The clerk of court collects the tax when recording. Ask your closing agent to apply the rate to your price in writing.

How does the Broward County tax cycle affect a seller?

The Broward appraiser values property on January 1 and takes exemption filings through March 1. Its site gives 954-357-6830 for questions.

  • August brings the proposed tax notice.
  • November bills carry the largest early payment discount, 4 percent.
  • April 1 marks delinquency.

Your closing agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer, so confirm the split reflects your exemption status.

Does homestead or portability matter if I leave Pembroke Pines?

It can, particularly after many years of ownership. Save Our Homes has kept your assessment growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and portability may move up to $500,000 of the savings to a new Florida home.

The new homestead has to begin within three years of the January 1 that follows the old one being given up. Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501 by March 1. The statute page notes later amendments first apply to the 2027 roll, so confirm current rules.

What if the house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?

Each situation runs on a clock. Estates with up to $150,000 non-exempt can use summary administration, creditors file within three months of publication or 30 days of service, whichever is later, and foreclosure sales follow judgment by 20 to 35 days.

Tenants receive a 3 day nonpayment notice and 7 days to cure many breaches. These facts affect offers, so assemble the documents first.

How does Pembroke Pines handle public safety and services that buyers ask about?

The city's fire rescue department runs six stations, and Pembroke Pines became the South Region answering point in the Broward County Regional 911 system in 2014. The department earned a Class 1 ISO rating in 1998, which the city's history says only 57 of 44,000 departments held then.

Insurance rating and response data are useful to mention to buyers, and your agent can confirm the current rating for your address.

What about tax certificates and tax deeds in Pembroke Pines?

Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. After two years a holder can apply for a tax deed with a $75 application fee, and the clerk runs the auction.

The opening bid on a homestead includes one half of the latest assessed value. If you are behind, ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff and weigh a sale before a deed application.

  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Senior deferral uses Form DR-570 by March 31.

Can seniors and veterans cut a Pembroke Pines tax bill?

Owners 65 or older may get an additional exemption of up to $50,000 if the local ordinance allows and income is within limit. Disabled veterans may receive a $5,000 assessed value reduction, and veterans 65 or older with a service-connected disability may get a discount equal to the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may receive an exemption proportional to the time deployed, and may rent out a homestead without abandoning it. Ask the property appraiser about proof needed.

What are the risks of an informal family transfer in Pembroke Pines?

Moving legal or beneficial title counts as a change of ownership for assessment, with exceptions for spouses and some transfers at death, and quit claim deeds carry stamp tax.

The statute wants a written conveyance signed before two witnesses, so have a title agent prepare it.

What steps lead from offer to closing in Pembroke Pines?

Once you accept, a title agent searches title, gathers payoffs and drafts the deed, which needs two witnesses. The clerk then records it and collects the tax.

  • Put the doc stamp payer in the contract.
  • Order mortgage payoff and association statements.
  • Check your exemption status before the tax split.
  • Have permit and inspection records ready for the buyer inspector.

Pembroke Pines is one of the largest of more than 400 Florida municipalities, so recent sales near you should be plentiful and easy to compare.

Which services and amenities do Pembroke Pines buyers ask about?

The city says it counts 41 arts and cultural facilities, plus parks, golf courses and tree lined neighborhoods. It cites recognition as an All-America City and describes its mission as fostering a place to live, work and raise a family.

Its fire rescue department began as a volunteer group in 1953, hired its first three full-time employees in 1973 and today serves from six stations. The city history also records Station 69 opening in 1978 and Station 101 with a communications center in 2001. Buyers care about response times and insurance ratings, so ask your insurer what rating applies to your address, and keep the answer with your sale documents for buyers who ask later.

What steps should I take to prepare a Pembroke Pines sale?

Start with paperwork. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill, any association documents, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions.

Then weigh a listing, a private sale and a cash offer by your net proceeds. Insist on a written offer and read every line.

More questions about Pembroke Pines, FL

What year did Pembroke Pines incorporate?

1960, on January 16 by the city's account, when it was a village of about 1,500 people.

Which doc stamp rate does Pembroke Pines use?

Seventy cents per $100 of consideration paid, because Broward is not Miami-Dade, as the state revenue page lists.

Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings?

Possibly. Portability may carry as much as $500,000 of the difference to a new Florida homestead.

Who pays the deed tax?

Under the state rule each party stays liable, so write the payer into the contract.

Is an inherited Pembroke Pines house taxed when it transfers?

Deeds from a personal representative under a probated will are listed as untaxed, while other transfers can be taxed, so check with a title agent.

Selling a house in Hollywood FAQ

How much is a house worth in Hollywood?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Hollywood at $374,200.

Which selling routes work best in Hollywood, FL?

Hollywood owners generally weigh a retail listing, a cash buyer and an as-is purchase. Which one fits depends on repair needs, your deadline, and whether a lender or a court date is setting the pace.

A listing reaches the most shoppers but adds showings, buyer financing and appraisal risk. A cash deal drops most of those conditions. Both end the same way at the Broward County records office: a witnessed deed, the transfer tax, and recording.

  • Agent listing: more exposure, slower, dependent on the buyer's loan.
  • Cash or as-is buyer: fewer conditions, no repair list, quicker signing.
  • Sale to a relative: still a transfer for consideration, so tax and homestead rules apply.

What makes Hollywood a distinct place to sell a house?

The city sits in southeastern Broward County between Miami and Fort Lauderdale. Its own website puts it at about 30 square miles and calls it Broward's third-largest municipality, while the Census Bureau counted 153,067 people in 2020 and estimates 157,019 for mid-2025.

Joseph Wesley Young planned the place, and a charter incorporated it on November 28, 1925. He laid three circles along a central boulevard, and one of them, Young Circle, now holds the ArtsPark in the downtown core. A hurricane on September 18, 1926 ended the first boom overnight. The city's history says the population dropped from roughly 18,000 to roughly 2,500, and that Hallandale and Dania left the city. Waterfront Broward has always swung with storms and credit.

Census QuickFacts shows homeowners occupying 58.9 percent of housing for 2020 to 2024, with $410,600 as the median home value and $1,653 as median rent. About four in ten households rent, so many sellers here are landlords, which changes both tax treatment and the closing checklist.

Which Hollywood areas and employers shape buyer demand?

Buyers sort the city into three areas: the barrier island along the Atlantic, the historic downtown around Harrison Street and Young Circle, and the western Hollywood Hills section that grew after Hollywood Boulevard was extended toward U.S. 27 in 1954.

  • Beach: the Broadwalk runs nearly 2.5 miles, with resort towers, condos and small inns.
  • Downtown: a mix of arts venues, bars and restaurants.
  • Employers: Memorial Regional Hospital, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Port Everglades (about 80 percent inside city limits) and the airport next door.

The city lists I-95, the Florida Turnpike and Tri-County Commuter Rail among its links. Census data gives workers a mean trip of 29.4 minutes. The School Board of Broward County runs the public schools within city limits, which number more than 30 including charters, and the city names Barry University and Nova Southeastern University among nearby higher-education sites.

How has Hollywood changed in ways that touch home values?

Public spending and big private projects have reshaped parts of the city since the 2000s. Voters approved a $54 million general obligation bond in 2004 for public safety and parks, and a $165 million bond in 2019 for safety, technology, parks, neighborhood work and resilience. The city says more than 30 projects were under construction under the later bond and that it bought more than 45 acres of open space.

  • Hollywood Beach: the Broadwalk was renovated in the early 2000s, utilities went underground, and Charnow Park and a Garfield Street parking garage followed.
  • Corridors: the city is rebuilding main roads with bike lanes, wider sidewalks and bus bays under a Complete Streets approach.
  • Nature: the Anne Kolb Nature Center preserves more than 1,500 acres of mangroves in the West Lake area.

The Seminole Indian Reservation lies inside city limits as a politically independent entity, and the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino has added a large hotel tower. Sellers near the beach, downtown or a rebuilt corridor can point buyers to these projects, while owners in other parts of the city should ask a local agent how nearby streets compare.

How does homestead status change a Hollywood sale?

If you live in the house, your exemption stops at sale, and the buyer files fresh. Broward's property appraiser says a seller's exemptions do not stretch past the year of sale.

The state also resets assessed value after a change of ownership, so the buyer's first bill can run above yours. Buyers know that, and it can surface in price talks. If you are moving to another Florida home, ask the appraiser about portability, which lets you carry part of your capped-value savings forward, provided you file a homestead application first. The appraiser prints March 1 as the timely date and September 20, 2027 as the last possible late-filing day for tax year 2027.

Landlords should heed one more warning from the same page: if a homestead house is rented, the exemption can be lost, and unreported changes can bring back taxes for up to ten years plus a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

What fees come due when a Hollywood deed changes hands?

The main item is the state deed tax. Section 201.02 sets it at 70 cents per $100 of the price, and the revenue department says every party named on the document is liable regardless of who agreed to pay. Consideration counts a mortgage on the property even when the buyer does not assume it.

The Broward clerk collects the tax at recording. Clerk charges under section 28.24 begin at $5.00 for a first page, with add-ons for extra pages, extra names and technology; ask your closing agent for the final figure on your deed.

Property taxes follow a separate calendar. Value is set on January 1, the bills come in November, a sliding discount applies to early payment, and anything unpaid goes delinquent April 1. Your closing agent splits the year between you and the buyer.

Which Hollywood dates and amounts are worth noting?

Homestead filingMarch 1 timely; Sept. 20, 2027 last late filing for 2027Broward Property Appraiser
Deed tax70 cents for each $100 of considerationSection 201.02

What if the Hollywood house faces foreclosure, probate or tenant issues?

  • Foreclosure: once a final judgment issues, the clerk's public sale comes 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff allows longer. Selling beforehand can keep that sale from happening.
  • Probate: a smaller estate can use summary administration (up to $150,000 non-exempt, or a death more than two years back). A lawyer should map creditor-claim deadlines first.
  • Tenants: month-to-month occupants get at least 30 days' notice to end the tenancy, and a nonpayment demand is a three-day written notice.

No Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004.

What should I gather before asking for a Hollywood cash offer?

  • Recorded deed and latest tax bill.
  • Payoff letters for each mortgage or lien, and association estoppel details for condos and HOAs.
  • Copies of leases and tenant contacts.
  • A list of known repairs, open permits and storm claims.
  • For an estate, the court's letters of administration.

A Florida land conveyance needs two subscribing witnesses, so schedule signing accordingly or use the audio-video witnessing the statute permits.

More questions about Hollywood, FL

Can I sell a Hollywood house with no repairs?

Yes. Cash and as-is buyers accept the condition you have and price it in. A retail buyer's lender may still ask for fixes.

Who covers the deed tax in Hollywood?

Your contract decides who actually pays. The state treats every party to the deed as liable at 70 cents per $100, so confirm the line item with your closing agent.

Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. Broward's appraiser says exemptions end with the year of sale, and the buyer applies on their own.

What if back taxes are owed on my Hollywood home?

They are normally paid from proceeds at closing once the Broward tax collector supplies a payoff amount. Unpaid balances turn delinquent April 1.

How soon can a Hollywood sale close?

Timing rests on title work, liens and the buyer. A cash buyer skips loan underwriting, but payoffs and recording still take days. Ask for a written timeline.

Selling a house in Gainesville FAQ

How much is a house worth in Gainesville?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Gainesville at $235,000.

How can a Gainesville owner sell?

A Gainesville seller can put the property up for sale, find a buyer without an agent, or sell for cash and skip repairs. The right pick turns on condition, tenants and deadline.

  • Agent listing: a big audience, plus showings and a lender to satisfy.
  • Direct sale: you own pricing and every form.
  • Cash: few conditions, negotiable timing, a price that allows for repairs.

Judge each bid by the money you keep once liens, tax and recording are paid. Gainesville covers 63.15 square miles of land at 2,234 people per square mile, so a house in one part of town can face a different buyer pool than a house in another. Ask each buyer how they arrived at a number, what they assume about repairs, and who covers closing items, and keep every offer in writing, dated and signed, so you can compare them side by side later. If an offer asks you to leave a deposit, sign over title early or pay a fee up front, stop and have an attorney read it first.

What do Gainesville's housing numbers look like?

Only 37.7 percent of Gainesville housing units are owner-occupied, so this is a renter-heavy city compared with most Florida places.

The mid-point value of an owner-occupied Gainesville home is $247,500 for 2020 to 2024, while rent sits at $1,296 in the middle, and 59,816 households with 2.14 persons each. Among residents, 13.1 percent of residents are under 18 and 11.9 percent are 65 or older. Of adults 25 and older, 53.7 percent hold a four-year degree or more, and the average commute is 18.8 minutes.

What does the Gainesville economy mean for house buyers?

QuickFacts shows 2022 receipts of $4,318,602 thousand in the health care and social assistance sector and retail sales of $3,578,831 thousand, so medical and retail work sit large in the local economy. Accommodation and food services sales were $716,783 thousand.

Household income in the middle is $46,195 in 2024 dollars and per capita income is $30,051, while 30.8 percent of persons are in poverty. Price matters to many local buyers, and rent matters to many local owners. The city counts 5,976 veterans for 2020 to 2024, and state guidance on veteran property tax benefits, such as the $5,000 assessed-value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember with a rating of 10 percent or more.

For a seller, the lesson is practical. Price the house against what local households can pay, and expect investors to run the rent against the value before they bid.

What should a Gainesville seller gather before closing?

A complete file shortens the path to closing and gives any buyer fewer reasons to renegotiate.

  • Proof of who may sign: deed, trust papers or probate order.
  • Payoff letters for each mortgage, lien or judgment recorded in Alachua County.
  • Lease copies, deposit records and rent history for any tenant.
  • Repair and permit records for roof, plumbing, electrical and air conditioning work.
  • Your TRIM notice and latest tax bill.

Under s. 689.01, a deed needs two subscribing witnesses at signing. Book the signing with your title agent so a notary and witnesses are present, and ask for a written estimate of your costs and net before you commit.

Why does a landlord-heavy market matter when you sell a Gainesville house?

With roughly six in ten households renting, many buyers are investors, and many sellers are landlords. A rented house sells differently from an empty one.

Census data finds 69.2 percent of residents at their address one year before the survey, so almost a third had moved. With that much movement, buyers want rent rolls, lease end dates and maintenance records.

A tenancy by the month ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period under s. 83.57. A written lease generally carries over to the buyer. Decide early whether you will deliver the house vacant or with the tenant in place, and say so in every conversation with a buyer.

What are the Gainesville rental rules for owners?

The city adopted a Rental Housing Ordinance on September 17, 2020 that set annual permits, inspections and property standards for residential rentals, and its own page now says the ordinance is being repealed.

That page adds that no specific rental regulations apply in Gainesville at present, though rentals must still meet the city's other ordinances. Check the Sustainable Development page for the current status before you describe the rule to a buyer, since an ordinance in repeal can change.

  • Rentals of fewer than 30 days: the city says these have not been regulated by the city since October 1, 2021.
  • Longer rentals: all other city codes still apply, such as property maintenance and code enforcement.

If you hold an older landlord permit, ask the city whether it needs to be closed or transferred.

What do deed recording and stamp tax add in Gainesville?

A Gainesville deed is taxed at 70 cents for every $100 of consideration, and the clerk in Alachua County collects it at recording.

Whoever signs the deed shares liability for the tax, whichever party the contract names as payer, and the clerk takes payment when the document is filed. The clerk's recording fee under s. 28.24(13) is charged page by page, with extra trust fund and technology charges on top. A title agent prints the full figure in the closing statement, so ask for it before signing.

How do Alachua County tax dates play into a sale?

Value is set each January 1, proposed-tax notices arrive in August, and bills follow in November.

The appraiser's August notice opens a 25 day window for a value petition with the clerk. Bills carry a 4 percent discount in November, falling a point each month through February. Taxes become delinquent on April 1. Homestead filings are due March 1, and a change of ownership resets the assessed value to just value the next January 1.

The closing agent splits the year's tax between seller and buyer, and the Alachua County tax collector can state the balance owed.

What if the Gainesville house is inherited or heading to foreclosure?

Florida law sets clear steps in both cases.

  • Inheritance: small or older estates may use summary administration (s. 735.201), and creditors face a filing cutoff under s. 733.702.
  • Foreclosure: after final judgment the clerk auctions the property on a fixed schedule (s. 45.031).

Talk to a probate or foreclosure attorney about your rights. A sale before the auction can protect equity that an auction might not.

More questions about Gainesville, FL

Is Gainesville mostly renters?

Mostly, yes. The Census reports a 37.7 percent owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024, so close to two thirds of households rent. Anyone selling a rental should expect buyers to ask for lease dates and rent amounts, and anyone selling a lived-in house is part of a smaller pool.

Does Gainesville regulate short-term rentals?

The city's page says rentals under 30 days have not been regulated by the city since October 1, 2021. Check county and state rules separately.

Are Gainesville rental permits still required?

The city says its 2020 Rental Housing Ordinance is being repealed and that no specific rental regulations apply now. Confirm the current status with the city before relying on that.

Who pays doc stamps on a Gainesville sale?

All parties to the deed are liable by statute. The contract normally says who pays, and the closing agent collects it at recording.

When are Alachua County taxes due?

Bills go out in November with early-payment discounts that shrink through February, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1.

How did Palm Bay grow into Brevard's largest city?

Palm Bay grew mostly in the last half century. The city's history page traces it to the settlement of Tillman at the mouth of Turkey Creek in 1887, renamed Palm Bay in 1925, and incorporated as a city in 1960 with 2,808 residents.

The city also records $13 million in damage and debris cleanup from hurricanes Charley, Frances and Jeanne in 2004. Storm history is a normal part of buyer and insurer conversations here.

How did the 2026 flood change selling in Palm Bay?

It added paperwork and, for some owners, financial help. The city's flood page, last updated November 12, 2026, describes road closures, a damage reporting form run by Brevard County Emergency Management, and waived permit fees for residential flood repairs.

  • Fee waiver: the Building Department said it would waive permit fees for flood-related home repairs. Call 321-953-8924 before starting work.
  • Insurance claims: an owner with a National Flood Insurance Program policy needs a substantial damage inspection as part of the claim and before permitting.
  • Disaster Relief Program: the city describes repair help for owners who have lived with a homestead exemption for a year or more, are current on mortgage, taxes and utilities, and have very low or low income. Aid above $20,000 comes as a forgivable 0 percent mortgage over five years.
  • Contractors: the city warns against paying everything upfront and points owners to the state's license lookup.

If your house took on water, an as-is cash sale can spare you a repair project and a permit file. If you repair first, keep photos, estimates and permits together, since a buyer's lender and insurer will ask for them.

What should a Palm Bay seller know about flood zones?

Palm Bay sits between the Indian River Lagoon on its east edge and the St. Johns River and marsh to the west, and the city's flood page says both can pose hazards in severe rain. The same page says that historically even major storms caused little structural flood damage, which makes the 2026 event stand out.

  • Flood map change: a new FEMA map took effect March 17, 2014, and the city says about 2,000 structures and over 5,000 residential lots left the Special Flood Hazard Area. Owners of those homes qualify for a Preferred Risk policy if they choose.
  • Insurance discount: the city holds a Community Rating System rating of 7, which it describes as a 15 percent reduction in federal flood insurance for residents.
  • Elevation certificates: the Building Department keeps copies of floodplain reviews with FEMA Elevation Certificates for homes built since 1993.
  • Map amendments: a raised structure can seek a Letter of Map Amendment or a Letter of Map Revision based on Fill. FEMA's fee for the second was $425 on the city's page.
  • Mandatory coverage: a federally backed mortgage on a building in the Special Flood Hazard Area requires a flood policy.

A buyer's lender will check the flood zone, so gather any elevation certificate and map amendment before you list. For zone questions, the Growth Management Department takes calls at 321-952-3400, extension 5246.

What does Palm Bay require for permits?

More than people expect. The city's permit FAQ lists carports, fences, sheds, re-roofing, window and door replacement, air conditioner change-outs, electrical, plumbing, gas work and generators.

Starting without a permit can bring a penalty of up to four times the fees. Residential permits average 14 working days for approval, and applications go through an online portal. An owner-builder permit is allowed only when the property will not be for sale or lease for a year, which matters if you plan to renovate and then sell soon after.

How do Brevard County taxes affect a Palm Bay sale?

The Brevard County Property Appraiser values property each January 1, and bills reach owners in November. The appraiser's site lists a 2026 homestead filing deadline of midnight on Monday, March 2, since March 1 landed on a Sunday that year.

  • The first $25,000 of a homestead exemption reaches all taxes, school taxes included. Up to $25,000 more reduces non-school taxes on value over $50,000.
  • The appraiser's home page carries a notice about Amendment 3 and major homestead exemption changes. Read it before filing.
  • Early payers get 4 percent off in November, falling to 1 percent in February.
  • Bills left unpaid go delinquent on April 1.

What if taxes go unpaid or the owner has died?

A tax certificate sale follows delinquency, and a tax deed can follow later. The collector sells certificates by June 1 to the bidder accepting the lowest interest rate, and a homestead with under $250 owed goes to the county rather than auction. The holder may apply for a deed once two years have passed, and the opening bid on a homestead includes half its latest assessed value. Selling first keeps your equity, since the closing agent pays the delinquent amount from proceeds.

For an estate, summary administration fits non-exempt assets up to $150,000 or a death more than two years back. For a lender case, a show cause hearing comes no sooner than 20 days after the order is served or 45 days after the complaint, and a judicial sale waits at least 20 days after final judgment. Brevard County's Clerk of the Circuit Court keeps these files.

What does a deed cost in Palm Bay?

Brevard County charges the state's 70 cents per $100 of price in stamps, collected by the clerk at recording. The title agent lists stamps and recording fees on the settlement statement, so ask for it ahead of closing day.

More questions about Palm Bay, FL

Are Palm Bay permit fees waived for flood repairs?

The city said it would waive permit fees for residential flood-related repairs after the 2026 flood. Call the Building Department at 321-953-8924 to confirm what applies to your address.

Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Palm Bay?

Yes. Florida does not bar the sale, and an as-is cash sale avoids the repair project. If you have a flood insurance claim, finish the substantial damage inspection first.

Who qualifies for the city's Disaster Relief Program?

The city page lists a one-year ownership requirement, a homestead exemption, current mortgage, tax and utility payments, and very low or low income. Call 321-726-5633 for current details.

What is the deed stamp rate in Brevard County?

70 cents per $100 of price. Miami-Dade is the only county that differs.

Does my homestead savings pass to the buyer?

No. The next January 1 resets the assessed value to just value. You may carry part of your savings to a new Florida homestead through portability, using form DR-501T within three years.

How much is a house worth in Miramar?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Miramar at $420,300.

Why does a Miramar house sale involve both the city and the county?

Miramar is a large city at the southwest edge of Broward County, and a house here is assessed by the Broward County Property Appraiser while the city adds its own fees to the bill. The city's about page lists a population of 137,107 and a land area of 31 square miles.

Its limits are Pembroke Road on the north, County Line Road or Honey Hill Road on the south, U.S. Highway 441 (State Road 7) on the east, and a line half a mile west of U.S. Highway 27 at the Everglades Conservation Area on the west. The city motto is "Beauty and Progress."

For a seller, the size means neighborhoods differ a lot in age, homeowners association rules and flood exposure, so the first step is to pull your own permit and lien history rather than relying on a citywide average.

How did Miramar grow from a tiny town into a big city?

Miramar was incorporated on May 26, 1955, with fewer than 200 residents and about 2.9 square miles. Its first boundaries ran from Southwest 64th Avenue on the east to University Drive on the west, between the Dade County line and Pembroke Road.

The city history page says the name means "Look at the Sea" in Spanish and was taken from an exclusive suburb of Havana. The first mayor and council were sworn in on June 20, 1955, appointed by the Governor, and the first municipal election followed in January 1959. The city has since grown to roughly 31 square miles, which is why a house built in the 1960s and one built decades later can sit within a few miles of each other and face different permit and records situations.

What does Miramar charge on a property tax bill?

The city's Management and Budget page says the Broward County Property Appraiser sets assessed value, several taxing authorities set rates, and real property taxes are collected annually beginning November 1. It states that 35 cents of each ad valorem tax dollar goes to the city and 65 cents to other Broward taxing agencies.

The millage on that page is a proposal, so ask the Broward tax office or the city for the adopted rate for the year of your closing. The fire and stormwater charges are non-ad valorem assessments that appear on the same bill but do not depend on your home's value. The city also runs a fire fee hardship exemption for qualified homeowners with a set application window each year.

How do permits and records affect a Miramar sale?

Miramar takes building permit applications through an online portal that is open at all hours, with counter help on limited weekdays. The Building Division says a residential permit usually takes about 15 business days to issue, and building fees carry an 8 percent surcharge.

Records matter at closing. The city states it is not likely to hold blueprints for homes more than 10 years past their certificate of occupancy, because state records rules let it discard residential plans after that. If you did work years ago, search for the permit now so a buyer's inspector does not find an open or expired one.

  • Call the Building Division at 954-602-3200 before starting a home improvement project.
  • An electric vehicle charger at home needs a city permit and inspection, even under a utility install program.
  • Homes in an association need association approval and a city permit for an EV charger.
  • Code case status can be checked online only by people listed as contacts on the case.

The city also offers a lien search, and the page notes that payments by check for lien searches must match the exact amount. Order one early so no lien shows up for the first time on the settlement statement.

How do Florida tax and recording rules apply to a Miramar closing?

Broward deeds carry the base statewide stamp rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, which the state revenue department states that is paid to the county clerk at recording. All parties to the deed are liable for it, so the contract should name who pays.

  • Homestead filings reach the property appraiser by March 1, and the city page lists the Broward office at 954-357-6830 for exemption questions.
  • The state's TRIM notice comes in August, and a value petition is due with the clerk within 25 days.
  • The early payment discount drops from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.
  • Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold by June 1.

A sale resets a homesteaded property's assessment to just value on the next January 1, so a buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours. A tax certificate holder cannot demand payment from an owner until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, but a tax deed application can follow, so clear delinquent taxes before listing.

What are my choices if I need to sell a Miramar house fast?

Miramar sellers tend to compare a listing, a direct sale and a cash bid, with condition, loan payoff and deadline driving the decision. A cash offer usually trims weeks off the timeline but comes at a lower price than a retail sale, so get more than one written number.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, with repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale to an investor: as-is purchase and a flexible closing date.
  • Short sale or pre-foreclosure sale: needs lender approval and starts before a judgment.

If a lender has filed suit, Florida's rules call for a sale date 20 to 35 days after final judgment, a 5 percent bidder deposit, and a 10 day objection window. Selling earlier gives you control over the price.

What should I collect before accepting an offer on a Miramar house?

Gather the items that decide your net proceeds before you sign anything, because Miramar has several charges that sit outside the base tax rate.

  • The current fire assessment and stormwater charges from your tax bill, since the city prints $479.21 a year for a residential unit and $120 per equivalent residential unit of 3,619 square feet.
  • Your homestead or other exemption status from the Broward County Property Appraiser.
  • A city lien search and a list of permits pulled on the property.
  • Association documents and any balance owed, if the home is in a community with dues.

The city's budget page also points out that the fire assessment helps maintain fire ratings that can lower property insurance costs. A buyer's agent may bring that up, so know your insurance declaration page before negotiating.

More questions about Miramar, FL

Who sets the property tax rate for a Miramar house?

Several taxing authorities do, and the Broward County Property Appraiser sets the assessed value. The city page shows a proposed city millage of 7.1172, so confirm the adopted figure with the city or the Broward tax collector.

How long does a Miramar building permit take?

About 15 business days for residential projects, according to the Building Division's page. Commercial projects are listed at about 30 business days.

Will a buyer ask for permit records on my Miramar home?

Not as a general rule, but a buyer's inspector may ask for permits on past work. The city says it is not likely to keep plans for homes more than 10 years past the certificate of occupancy.

What is the Miramar fire assessment?

It is a yearly non-ad valorem fee on the property tax bill that pays for fire and emergency resources. The city prints $479.21 per year for a residential unit, and a hardship exemption is available for qualified homeowners.

Where can I check for liens before selling in Miramar?

Use the city's lien search through its Financial Services pages and ask your title company for a full title search. Pay for the lien search in the exact amount the page requires.

How does the Broward County Property Appraiser affect a Coral Springs sale?

What if you owe more than you can pay in Coral Springs?

Selling before the judgment date can keep the proceeds in your hands.

How do inherited or rented Coral Springs houses differ?

An occupied rental brings extra steps: monthly tenancies need 30 days' notice, and a rent demand gives 3 days, excluding weekends and court holidays. Once a court rules for the landlord, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice. Coral Springs also has a large renter share, with 39.7 percent of housing units rented.

What relief exists for older owners and veterans in Coral Springs?

Selling a house in West Palm Beach FAQ

How much is a house worth in West Palm Beach?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in West Palm Beach at $369,800.

How can a West Palm Beach owner close quickly?

The two fastest routes are selling straight to a cash buyer or investor and a short listing priced to move. A West Palm Beach seller who needs certainty on timing usually weighs three things: price, days to close, and how much repair work the buyer will demand.

  • Cash or investor sale: the buyer buys as-is and the closing date is often your choice.
  • Agent listing: a wider buyer pool and often a higher price, with showings and lender timelines.
  • Hybrid: list first, then take a cash offer if the market response is slow.

Ask each buyer how they handle title problems, who orders the title search, and what happens to the deposit if the buyer backs out. In West Palm Beach, where many houses date from earlier decades, those terms matter as much as the number on the first page. Compare offers on what you net after the deed tax, title charges, any unpaid taxes and a rental license filing if the house is let to tenants. A higher headline price can net less than a lower cash offer once those lines are added.

What is West Palm Beach and why does its housing mix matter to a seller?

As the seat of Palm Beach County, West Palm Beach has a record the city's history page sums up: it was incorporated on November 5, 1894, two years before Miami. It reports roughly 1,000 residents in 1895 and an estimated population of 120,000 or more.

The same page lists the places buyers know: The Square, Clematis Street, Antique Row and Northwood Village, plus the Kravis Center, the Norton Museum of Art and the Grassy Waters Everglades Preserve on the western edge. It also notes that Palm Beach Junior College, Florida's first junior college, opened in 1933 and that thousands of servicemen passed through the city's airport in World War II.

That age shows in the housing stock. Historic neighborhoods sit alongside newer waterfront and downtown buildings. An older house may carry deferred maintenance, so an as-is sale can save a seller the cost of repairs before listing.

Does West Palm Beach require a rental license when a house changes hands or leased?

Yes. The city's Rental Property Guidelines say all rental units must secure a rental tax application, whether the unit is a short-term listing on a platform like Airbnb or a lease to a tenant, and that processing generally takes seven to 10 business days.

Owners are also asked to complete a zoning review that verifies the number of units, and the page lists interior and exterior conditions inspectors look for, such as working appliances, window screens, paved parking and visible address numbers. After applying, the owner contacts Code Enforcement at (561) 822-1465.

Rental property types in West Palm Beach, as the city's guidelines define them
TypeDescriptionExtra requirement noted
Type 1Owner-occupied single-family, multifamily or duplexProof the property is owner-occupied; owner name must match the recorded deed
Type 2Not owner-occupied single-family or duplexEntire dwelling unit rented
Type 3Not owner-occupied multifamily, such as apartments or condosBuilding and unit counts; compliance with any geographic caps

If you sell a rental, tell the buyer which type applies. The page ties the ownership on the application to the deed recorded with the Palm Beach County Clerk's Office, so a new owner has to apply in their own name.

How do code enforcement and permits affect a West Palm Beach sale?

Open violations and unpermitted additions can slow a closing. Rental owners must hold a license and pass an inspection under the city's guidelines, so an extra unit added to a structure without paperwork is a likely sticking point.

The Rental Property Guidelines also say the code compliance division sets minimum standards for substandard housing conditions, trash and debris, yard upkeep and parking areas.

Before you list, walk the lot for visible issues, check that any garage conversion or added unit has paperwork, and ask Code Enforcement about open cases on the address. A buyer paying cash can take a property with problems, but the price will reflect the cleanup.

What are the West Palm Beach tax due dates and early-payment discounts?

Palm Beach County mails the bills, and the County Tax Collector says that by November 1 it sends more than 600,000 property tax bills, payable from November 1 through March 31. The Property Appraiser sends the proposed-tax notice each August.

  • November: 4 percent discount
  • December: 3 percent discount
  • January: 2 percent discount
  • February: 1 percent discount
  • March: no discount; April 1: taxes become delinquent

The tax collector's page adds that delinquent tax cannot be paid online and that postmark date is not proof of payment once a tax is delinquent. It also says a bill sent to a seller after a sale should be forwarded to the new owner, or the office can be told through a Property Sold Form. Questions about mailing address or exemptions go to the Property Appraiser at (561) 355-2866, and delinquent amounts to the Tax Collector at (561) 355-2264.

Your bill includes non-ad valorem charges as well as ad valorem tax. The county gives the Solid Waste Authority fee as an example, set by the type of property.

Can a West Palm Beach homeowner defer or limit property taxes?

Some owners can. State revenue guidance describes a homestead tax deferral filed on Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31, and installment plan applications due by the following May 1.

Non-homestead property has its own protection: assessed value growth is limited to 10 percent each year. For homestead, the Save Our Homes cap holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and the cap resets when title changes. A buyer of your house may therefore see a higher assessment the following January 1 than you did.

A West Palm Beach seller who moves within Florida may carry some of that savings forward. Portability has a three year window counted from the January 1 that follows abandonment of the old homestead, and Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501 by March 1.

What do deed and recording costs look like when selling in West Palm Beach?

Deeds carry a state tax of $0.70 per $100 of price, and since Palm Beach County is not Miami-Dade, the Miami-Dade rate stays out of the picture. State guidance makes every party to the deed liable, though the contract decides who pays.

The clerk's recording fee is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages under the statute, with a $1.00 first-page and $0.50 later-page trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge. Request a full settlement statement before you sign so each line is visible.

How long does the West Palm Beach rental license take?

The city says it is generally processed in seven to 10 business days. A zoning review of the unit count is part of the process.

When do West Palm Beach property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Palm Beach County's tax collector says delinquent tax cannot be paid online and postmark date no longer counts as proof of payment.

Which discount applies if I pay in December?

A 3 percent discount applies for December payment, per the Palm Beach County Tax Collector. November is 4 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent.

Must I pull a permit for repairs I make before selling?

In many cases. Florida's 2026 permit exemption for projects under $7,500 has limits, and electrical, plumbing and structural work still need permits. Ask the city's Development Services staff before starting work.

Selling a house in Lakeland FAQ

How much is a house worth in Lakeland?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Lakeland at $229,100.

How can I sell my Lakeland house on a short timeline?

Three routes are open to a Lakeland owner: sell to a cash buyer, hire an agent, or go it alone. The cash route wins on speed, since nobody is waiting on a lender and the buyer takes the property with its flaws.

A listing may attract a higher bid, yet it asks you to prepare the house, host showings and absorb inspection requests. If the house is packed with an estate's belongings, has a dated interior or needs a new roof, that preparation can drag on for months. A turnkey house with a flexible timeline is the better fit for the open market.

  • Cash: skip repairs, choose the closing day.
  • Agent listing: broader audience, longer timeline.
  • Sale by owner: you carry the paperwork and negotiation.

What should I know about Lakeland's lakes before I list?

Water defines the city. Lakeland says it has 38 named lakes plus many smaller ones, ranging from 2.5 acres at Lake Blanton to 2,272 acres at Lake Parker, and the city limits cover 75.16 square miles.

Natural lakes include Parker, Hunter, Hollingsworth, Bonny, Beulah, Bonnet, Mirror, Morton, Gibson and Wire. Others, such as Bentley, Canyon, Crago, John, Waterview and Somerset, formed from phosphate mining. The city's public works page explains that all storm drains empty into a lake, pond, wetland or other waterway, and that the lakes help reduce local flooding. Discharge from them reaches tributaries of the Peace, Alafia and Hillsborough river systems. It also lists yard debris left in the street among illegal discharges, because clippings feed algae blooms.

Sellers have little to do here. Keep yard waste out of the street before photos are taken, and note any lake frontage in your own records. The city also runs a pollution hotline for reporting discharges, listed on its lakes and stormwater page.

Where did Lakeland come from?

Lakeland was incorporated on January 1, 1885. Founder Abraham Munn, from Louisville, bought 80 acres of today's downtown in 1882 and laid out the town two years later. Residents rejected Munnville, Red Bug and Rome City as names. A rival settlement named Acton once stood on the south side of Lake Parker and faded away by 1906.

The railroad and a 227 foot elevation helped the town thrive, and by the mid-1890s about 25 trains stopped each day. Strawberries, citrus and the Marsh seedless grapefruit shaped the early economy. Buildings from the 1920s boom, including the Terrace Hotel and Polk Theatre, are on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Detroit Tigers have trained here since 1934. After World War II, George Jenkins moved the Publix headquarters to the city. Florida Southern College moved to Lakeland in 1922 and, starting in 1938, Frank Lloyd Wright designed its campus, which the city calls the largest collection of his work in one place.

The preservation page points to landmarks across several eras: the 1928 Lake Mirror Promenade, a 1901 Craftsman bungalow on Lake Avenue, and the 1957 Southgate Shopping Center arch. The Polk County Tax Collector's Lakeland Service Center sits in a building constructed in 1953 as a Publix store, an example of an older building put to new use.

Is my Lakeland house inside a historic district?

Possibly. Lakeland has seven local historic districts covering 1.42 square miles, protecting more than 1,600 buildings and 13 landmarks, and the program dates to 1980.

The districts hold 7.15 percent of the city's parcels and about 6 percent of its residents. Recent resurveys documented 770 resources in the Dixieland and Munn Park districts and 1,042 in the East and South Lake Morton districts. For Munn Park, the report counted 66 contributing properties; for Dixieland, 466. Contributing status affects what exterior changes a buyer can make.

The city invites owners to email its historic preservation office to learn whether a home is a contributing structure, and the Lake Morton survey page offers an address lookup. Get that answer before you list, and include it in your disclosures to prospective buyers.

Those surveys also suggest where the rules may go. The Dixieland report recommends widening the district's period of significance to 1975, while Munn Park keeps its 1884 to 1946 window. If the Dixieland change is adopted, more mid-century houses could count as contributing, so ask the preservation office about the status of any house built before 1975.

  • Look up the address.
  • Ask about design review for windows, roofs and additions.
  • Save any approvals for past work.

What does Polk County do when a Lakeland tax bill goes unpaid?

A Polk real estate bill that is still open on April 1 of the year after assessment is delinquent.

The Polk County Tax Collector adds 3 percent interest and an advertising charge on that date. If June 1 arrives with the balance unpaid, the lien goes to an online auction where bidding opens at 18 percent and moves down. Such a certificate lapses at seven years, though its holder can seek a tax deed once two years have passed. Redeemers pay either the rate bid or a minimum 5 percent charge, whichever is higher, according to the collector's delinquency page.

Have your closing agent verify this year's bill and any older balance. Paying in November earns the 4 percent state discount, and homestead requests go to the property appraiser by March 1.

Source: Polk County Tax Collector delinquency and tax sale page.

What deed and transfer costs apply in Lakeland?

Polk County uses the standard Florida deed tax of 70 cents for every $100 of consideration.

Because the state holds every signer of the deed responsible for the tax, the contract's split is only a private understanding. Any mortgage on the property is part of consideration. Recording starts at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each further page, with extra statutory charges, and two witnesses must see the deed signed.

The sale closes out your homestead on this house. The buyer is assessed fresh the next January 1. Moving within Florida? Ask the property appraiser about portability, which has a March 1 filing date.

What if the Lakeland house is inherited or rented?

Establish who can sign first, then handle the occupants.

A streamlined court procedure exists for small estates, and for any estate once two years have passed since the death. A probate attorney can say whether it fits.

Renters on a monthly basis need 30 days' notice to end the tenancy.

  • Collect letters of administration or the death certificate.
  • Confirm tax status with the Polk tax collector.
  • Gather leases and notices for any tenant.

More questions about Lakeland, FL

How large is Lakeland?

The city says its limits cover 75.16 square miles, with 38 named lakes inside. Lake Parker is the biggest at 2,272 acres, and Lake Blanton the smallest named one at 2.5 acres.

Can a historic district block my sale?

No. It governs exterior changes, not who may buy. Ask the city's historic preservation office whether your house is a contributing structure and keep that answer with your sale papers.

What is a Polk tax certificate?

It is a lien that the tax collector auctions to an investor after the delinquency date, and it does not transfer the house. A holder can ask for a tax deed after two years, so pay the balance before you list.

Does a sale end my Florida homestead?

Yes, on that house. Portability may let you move part of your capped value to another Florida homestead.

Who pays the Florida deed tax?

The contract assigns it, though the state treats every party to the deed as liable. The Polk County rate is 70 cents for each $100.

Why does selling in Pompano Beach differ from selling elsewhere in Broward?

Pompano Beach is a beach city in the north of Broward County, and the city's own resident page says it spans over 25 square miles, halfway between Miami and Palm Beach. The same page counts over 101,400 residents for most of the year and over 150,000 once part-time owners return for winter.

That seasonal pulse shapes a sale. Showings pick up while snowbirds are in town, and an empty house can sit quietly through summer. Owners with deferred repairs, a tenant or an unpaid lien usually weigh three paths.

  • An agent listing, with repair requests, open houses and a closing date tied to the buyer's lender.

What local history and land use sit behind Pompano Beach neighborhoods?

Pompano was already a town when Broward County formed on October 1, 1915, and Broward had only three incorporated places that day: Dania, Pompano and Fort Lauderdale. The Florida East Coast Railway reached Palm Beach in 1894 and Miami in 1896, and farming settlements grew up along those tracks, Pompano among them.

Before that, Pompano belonged to Palm Beach County, which became Florida's 47th county on July 1, 1909 with Pompano as its southernmost town. Broward then split away partly over a dispute on alcohol sales and partly because northern Dade residents felt their tax dollars favored Miami, and the county takes its name from a governor who championed Everglades drainage, according to the city's historical pages.

A large piece of the city's layout comes from the Pompano Beach Air Park, which began as a World War II satellite training field for the naval air station at today's Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood airport. The city took it over on August 29, 1947, and the city's airport page says the Air Park now totals 650 acres after land went to schools, a mall site in 1968, a sports complex and a 2007 transfer that includes part of the golf course, Community Park and a fire station.

For a seller, that history shows up in a few concrete ways.

  • Properties near Copans Road and the NE 5th Avenue railway line sit in a mixed corridor of homes, parks and public facilities.
  • Buyers often ask about school zoning for Pompano Beach Elementary and Pompano Beach High, both built on former Air Park land.

How did Pompano Beach get its name and its housing mix?

The city's historical pages say a survey crew working for the canal and railway companies around 1880 wrote the word pompano on a map, and the settlement kept it. The town incorporated in 1908, and Beach joined the name on June 16, 1947, after the oceanfront settlement was annexed.

Growth came in layers. The Census Bureau counted 99,845 people in 2010 and 112,046 in 2020, then estimated 117,211 for July 2025. Older single-family blocks, mid-century duplexes and newer condo and townhome projects now share the same city, so a flat citywide price tells you little about one address.

The city markets its 1,000-foot fishing pier, redeveloped beachside fishing village and the early-1900s Hillsboro Lighthouse near the inlet. What does the Broward homestead exemption mean when I sell in Pompano Beach?

It ends with your ownership. Broward's property appraiser states that the seller's exemptions do not continue beyond the year of the sale, so the next occupant files fresh.

Broward lists a March 1 filing deadline each year, and September 20, 2027 as the hard late-filing cutoff for the 2027 year. The office warns that renting a house out would likely cost the exemption and that unreported changes can bring back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

Florida re-values a property after a change of ownership, so a buyer's first bill often runs above yours. The Department of Revenue says a sale, foreclosure or title transfer starts that reset, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses.

  • Keep the annual receipt Broward mails each January.
  • Cancel the exemption on a house you no longer occupy.
  • Ask about portability if you are moving to another Florida homestead within three tax years.

Do the November 2026 amendment results affect a Pompano Beach sale?

They can shape what buyers will pay. A Volusia property appraiser explainer reports that voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, lifting the non-school homestead exemption to as much as $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028, and cutting the non-homestead cap to 5 percent.

It adds that implementing legislation will settle some details, so ask Broward's property appraiser how the changes will reach your parcel.

What costs and paperwork come with a deed in Pompano Beach?

Florida taxes a deed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county but Miami-Dade. Every party to the document is liable, so the purchase contract settles who pays.

The Broward clerk records the deed and collects that tax. Section 28.24 sets a first-page recording charge of $5.00 and $4.00 per added page, before technology surcharges, so request a quote.

  • Obtain payoff statements from each mortgage and lien holder.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the Broward tax bill.
  • Check city permit and code records for open items.
  • Arrange two witnesses for the signing, which Florida requires for land conveyances.

What if the Pompano Beach house has tenants, a foreclosure case or an heir?

Each situation can sell, on its own clock. A month-to-month tenancy ends with 30 days' notice (section 83.57), and unpaid rent starts with a three-day written notice (section 83.56).

In foreclosure, the clerk's sale follows final judgment by 20 to 35 days unless extended (section 45.031). Closing first protects your equity.

For an heir, summary administration fits an estate of $150,000 or less, or a death over two years ago (section 735.201).

Often yes, since no lender appraisal is involved. Title must still be clear, with liens paid and the deed witnessed and recorded in Broward.

The sale contract decides, though the state holds every party liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade.

Will my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. Broward's property appraiser says it stops with the sale year, and the buyer applies anew before March 1.

Can I sell while I am behind on the mortgage?

Yes, if the closing beats the clerk's foreclosure sale. Move early, since that sale can come 20 to 35 days after judgment.

Which office records my deed?

At the Broward County clerk's office, which also collects stamp tax at recording. Bring the signed deed and the fee.

What drives the Clearwater economy that buyers come from?

Can a Clearwater landlord sell a rental house?

Yes. The city's Planning and Development Department publishes a Business Tax Receipt application for residential rentals, and it spells out what Clearwater expects of a rental. The form defines a residential use inside a residential zoning district excludes stays under 31 days or one calendar month, whichever is less.

An owner who rents by the night should read that wording before listing, since a buyer planning short stays will ask. The form also names the housing code items an inspector can review:

It also requires a local property manager with a street address in Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee or Sarasota County. Before a rental changes hands, ask Planning and Development about the current fee and the registration steps for the new owner.

What does Clearwater's code say about the outside of a house?

The same application lists exterior standards that code officers apply to any residential lot: abandoned vehicles, address numbers, debris, sound fences, graffiti, overgrown grass, outdoor storage, parking, lighting and trash facilities.

Walk the lot with that list before the first showing. A boat parked on the grass or a tall lawn can draw a complaint mid-sale, and a buyer's inspector will write up the same items. Fixing them is cheap next to a price reduction.

Which Pinellas County office handles value and exemptions for a Clearwater home?

The county property appraiser sets values, and the main office sits at 315 Court Street, 2nd floor, Clearwater, open weekdays from 8 AM to 5 PM. Its homepage counts 437,624 real property parcels, among them 408,947 residential parcels, 103,445 condo units and 44,323 manufactured home units.

Those counts show how often a Clearwater sale involves a condo or a manufactured home, each with separate paperwork. Under the state calendar, each parcel is valued on January 1, exemption applications close March 1, and proposed values come in an August TRIM notice. After a sale, a homestead is revalued at full just value starting the next January 1, because the sale counts as a change of ownership.

How are Florida taxes handled when a Clearwater house sells?

A Pinellas deed carries state tax of 70 cents per $100 of price. The statute makes each signer answerable, whichever one the contract names as payer, and the clerk takes payment at recording. Find that line on the settlement sheet before signing.

Tax bills are mailed in November. Paying in November earns a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent, and anything unpaid goes delinquent on April 1. If you close partway through the year, the title company divides the bill with the buyer, so ask how it will do the split.

What if a Clearwater owner is behind on the mortgage?

Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. The clerk schedules the auction between 20 and 35 days after the final judgment, though the lender may agree to a later date, and the winning bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit. If the house sells before that date, payoff comes from the proceeds and the case can close.

The certificate of title that follows an auction triggers deed tax measured on the top bid. Call your loan servicer or a Florida attorney soon, and set a cash offer beside a short sale before an auction date arrives.

What should a seller of an inherited Clearwater home do?

Settle who has authority first, because heirs cannot convey clean title on their own. An estate worth $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets can use summary administration, and so can an estate opened more than two years after the death. Under a probated will, the revenue department lists the representative's deed as free of deed tax.

Creditors lose their claims unless they file within three months of the first published notice, or 30 days after service on a creditor, whichever comes later. Florida levies no estate tax on deaths after 2004. The probate court clerk can say which path applies to this estate.

Can I sell a Clearwater house with tenants?

Yes. A sale does not cancel the lease by itself. Florida allows 3 days' written notice for unpaid rent and requires 30 days to end a tenancy that runs month to month, so the buyer either keeps the tenant or waits out proper notice.

What does the city require before a Miami Gardens house can transfer?

Miami Gardens requires a Certificate of Re-Occupancy before a property is purchased, sold, conveyed or transferred. That city step comes before closing, so build it into your timeline from day one.

The city's code compliance guide for property owners says the certificate takes five to seven business days when all information is provided. It exists to help the city track changes to structures, and it applies to every kind of sale, retail or investor.

  • Ask for the certificate early, before a contract deadline forces a scramble.
  • Gather the permits for past repairs and upgrades.
  • Ask the city whether open violations or liens are recorded against the parcel.

How does the Miami Gardens re-occupancy certificate work?

The owner applies through the city's code enforcement and business licensing office, which can be reached at reoccupancy@miamigardens-fl.gov. The city inspects for changes made without a permit, and altered space such as added square footage is reported to the county so the property record and taxes can be corrected.

Violations do not stop a sale. The guide says a sale can go ahead as long as the buyer signs a stipulation agreement with the city promising to fix the problems. That helps with tired houses, since a buyer willing to cure the violations can still close.

Unpermitted work is handled by legalizing it, which means securing a permit after the fact. The guide warns that this can bring penalties, and in the worst case demolition of the structure, so find out before you list.

What work in Miami Gardens needs a permit?

The city lists fences, hurricane shutters, door and window installations, sheds, screen enclosures, pool barriers, patio slabs, gazebos, plumbing and electrical work, air conditioner change-outs, room additions and sea walls. The list is not complete, so call the building department before assuming anything is exempt.

If you replaced an air conditioner, enclosed a patio or put up a shed, dig out the permit papers now. Gaps in that record are a likely reason an inspection drags on.

Other yard and street rules in the guide can also draw citations before a sale: open-air storage is prohibited, portable storage containers should be removed within thirty calendar days, and vehicles on the swale or public right of way may be towed. Clear those items before an inspector or buyer visits.

Do landlord rules affect a Miami Gardens house sale?

A house that is rented out carries a Landlord Permit requirement, renewable every year by March 31. The application needs the permit fee, the names and birthdates of all occupants, and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

A sitting tenant changes the sale. Florida's demand for unpaid rent runs 3 days, leaving out weekends and court holidays, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. After a court win, the sheriff restores possession once a 24-hour notice has been posted.

An investor may want the house empty, may keep the tenant, or may ask you to deliver it vacant. Write that choice into the contract so nobody guesses at closing.

What does Miami-Dade charge on a Miami Gardens deed?

Because Miami Gardens lies inside Miami-Dade, the county's own deed stamp applies: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cent surtax that a single-family-only transfer does not owe.

The clerk takes the tax at recording, and each signer shares liability. Warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds are all taxable, as is a deed given to a lender instead of foreclosure. Recording is priced per page under section 28.24, with added trust fund and technology charges.

How are Miami Gardens property taxes billed?

Miami-Dade's appraiser values the parcel and the county's tax collector issues the bill. The appraiser says it mails no bills and sets no taxes, and it certified its 2026 roll on October 16, 2026.

The state calendar starts with a January 1 valuation date and a March 1 exemption deadline, then proposed notices in August and bills in November. Late bills turn delinquent in April, and tax certificates follow by June.

After a sale the buyer is assessed at full value from the next New Year's Day, and the seller's homestead exemption stops. A seller buying elsewhere in Florida can ask about portability, requested with the new homestead filing.

  • Have the closing agent prorate this year's bill between you and the buyer.
  • Check that no tax certificate has been sold against the parcel.
  • Ask the appraiser whether a city inspection changed the property record.

What if the Miami Gardens house is in foreclosure or probate?

Foreclosure follows the court's calendar. The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the lender agrees to wait, and after a sale homeowners are told to ask the clerk about surplus funds.

An inherited house may qualify for Florida's summary administration, which fits estates of up to $150,000 in non-exempt property or deaths over two years old. Creditors lose their claims after a statutory window that runs from the notice to creditors or from service on a known creditor.

Ask a Florida attorney or the clerk's self-help staff which papers a title insurer will require before it covers the sale.

What can I do about city liens on a Miami Gardens house?

The city's code compliance team lists a lien resolution service with four parts: lien searches, administrative release of a lien, lien amnesty and lien reduction, and registration of vacant and abandoned property through a third party.

Order a lien search early. A fine that has piled up from an old violation is the kind of surprise that shows up on a title report days before closing. If a lien exists, ask the city whether amnesty or reduction applies, and get the release in writing so the title company can record it.

Owners of a vacant house should also ask about the vacant property registration, since an empty, neglected house draws code attention. Mow, secure and clear the yard before a buyer or inspector visits.

How do I evaluate a cash offer in Miami Gardens?

Total up the cash you would keep after every cost, then read who handles the re-occupancy certificate, any city lien payoff and the deed stamp. An as-is investor should still state in writing who pays city fees and who signs the stipulation agreement.

Before signing, get the settlement date, the closing agent's name and the deposit terms in writing.

More questions about Miami Gardens, FL

Is a city certificate needed to transfer a Miami Gardens house?

Yes. The city's property owner guide says a Certificate of Re-Occupancy is required before the purchase, sale, conveyance or transfer of title of any real property, with a turnaround of five to seven business days when information is complete.

May a Miami Gardens house with open violations be sold?

Yes, when the buyer signs a stipulation agreement promising the city to fix them, per the city's guide. Unpermitted work must be legalized through a permit.

When is the Miami Gardens landlord permit due?

It renews each year on or before March 31. The application needs the fee, all occupants' names and birthdates and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

What deed stamp tax applies in Miami Gardens?

Miami-Dade uses 60 cents per $100 and a 45 cent surtax, and a deed moving only a single-family home owes no surtax, as the state revenue department lists it.

Which office mails Miami Gardens property tax bills?

The Miami-Dade tax collector. The property appraiser assesses value and says it neither mails bills nor collects taxes.

Selling a house in Davie FAQ

How much is a house worth in Davie?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Davie at $433,600.

How can a Davie homeowner sell and walk away?

Three routes exist in Davie: hire an agent, sell without one, or take a cash purchase with no repairs on your side. Which one fits depends on the work the house needs and how soon the money matters.

Davie is a town in Broward County, and it behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Its own history is tied to ranching, citrus and horses. If your lot has a barn, fencing, a pool or other outbuildings, those extras shape what an inspector will flag, so plan for them from the start.

  • Agent route: the biggest audience, plus showings, an appraisal and a loan contingency.
  • Owner route: you draft the contract, give disclosures and coordinate the closing.
  • Cash route: no lender involved, common for inherited, rented or worn-out houses.

Where does Davie, FL get its western character?

Davie was incorporated on November 16, 1925, and the town marked its centennial with events from November 2024 through 2025. Early in the twentieth century it was known as Zona, settled by workers who were draining the Everglades, and it took its present name in 1916 from the developer R.P. Davie.

Agriculture shaped it from there. The Town describes Davie as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown. The Old Davie School Historical Museum, built in 1918, is the oldest permanent school building in Broward County, and the Orange Blossom Festival began in 1937 to honor the local citrus industry.

The heritage reaches into the rulebook. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage, so check with the Town on whether it touches exterior work on your parcel, particularly inside the western-themed district.

How big is Davie and who lives there?

The Town of Davie says it is home to more than 107,000 residents, and it describes a rural atmosphere, a western-themed district and a large educational complex as the traits that set it apart from other Broward municipalities.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A home on a half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Roof age, pool condition and any outbuildings are worth sorting out before showings.

If an association covers your property, ask for its governing documents early. In many communities a sale needs association approval, estoppel letters and a check for pending special assessments, and a slow reply can stall a closing longer than any repair.

Can you rent out a Davie house as a vacation rental instead?

Yes, but Davie regulates it through a registration program. Under the Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and section 509.242 of the Florida Statutes, a vacation rental is a unit rented to transient guests more than three times in a calendar year for periods under thirty days, or one that is advertised as regularly rented that way.

The Town requires a license from the state Department of Business and Professional Regulation before it will accept the application. The packet also asks for proof of ownership from the Broward County Property Appraiser, corporate documents if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

The Town lists a maximum civil penalty of up to $500 per violation. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before you advertise.

Which Davie offices and records will you need?

Three sources cover most of what a Davie seller needs. The Town's Police Code Compliance Division, at 1230 South Nob Hill Road, handles vacation rental registration and code questions, and its number is 954-693-8237. The Broward County Property Appraiser's website, BCPA.net, is where the Town expects owners to pull proof of ownership. If an LLC or corporation holds title, the Town asks for corporate documents from Sunbiz.org.

Gather those before a buyer's attorney asks. A clean ownership record, a current tax bill and written confirmation that no code case is open make a Davie contract easier to sign, and they are quick to collect when you know where each one lives.

Disabled veterans have one more item to keep handy. The Town's rental program requires a DD214 and disability documentation to apply a veteran exemption, and the same paperwork helps if a buyer asks about the state's assessment reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers.

What do Broward County property taxes mean for a Davie seller?

Your Davie property is valued and billed by Broward County on a state-set calendar: valuation on January 1, a proposed-tax notice in August and bills in November.

  • March 1 is the filing date for exemptions and classifications, which matters for a lot with an agricultural classification.
  • The clerk takes value petitions during the 25 days after the August notice.
  • Early payment discounts start at 4 percent in November and end at 1 percent in February.
  • Delinquency begins April 1.

Assessed value on non-homestead property may climb at most 10 percent a year, the state says. Homesteads have the Save Our Homes cap instead, set at 3 percent or the inflation change, whichever is lower. The cap ends at sale, and the buyer begins at just value.

If part of your land holds an agricultural classification, ask the property appraiser how a sale or change in use affects it before you commit to a contract.

What will the Davie deed transfer involve?

The Broward clerk handles recording, and Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The statute counts any mortgage or encumbrance on the land, assumed or not, so paying off a loan does not shrink the base as sellers sometimes hope.

Revenue officials say every party shares liability for the tax whoever agrees to bear it. Your contract assigns the cost, and the title company usually collects it.

Recording fees come on top. Section 28.24 prices the first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, plus per-page records-fund and technology charges. Spousal homestead deeds and divorce deeds for the marital home carry listed exemptions, so ask the title agent before assuming tax applies.

What if the Davie house is inherited, facing foreclosure or rented?

Florida law gives each of these a defined path, and a sale stays possible.

When an heir sells, the department lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable. Transfers made for estate planning are taxable, because it says no specific exemption covers them. Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004.

After a foreclosure judgment the clerk's sale must fall 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to extend it. A buyer who closes sooner pays the lender and leaves the owner whatever equity remains.

Unpaid rent calls for a written three-day demand, not counting weekends and court holidays. A tenant raising any defense besides payment must deposit the rent with the court within five days or give up those defenses.

More questions about Davie, FL

Does Davie require registration for short-term rentals?

Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

What is the Davie vacation rental fee?

A full registration year runs $500 and the half year from April 1 runs $300. Renewals cost $450 when the owner does not live there and $400 when the owner does.

Who records a deed for a Davie property?

The Broward clerk records it and takes the deed stamp tax of 70 cents per $100, and the title company usually arranges both.

What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?

The cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida homestead? Ask the Broward appraiser about portability.

Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?

Yes. A buyer may accept the lease as written. For a vacant house, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and only a sheriff can physically remove an occupant.

How much is a house worth in Palm Coast?
