The property appraiser's office in downtown Sanford sets assessed values, takes exemption applications and posts parcel and deed data. Its home page lists the office at 1101 E. 1st Street in Sanford, with weekday hours of 8 to 5 and a customer service line at 407-665-7506.

The 2026 tax roll statistics on that page show 181,187 real property parcels in the county, of which 138,250 are residential, with a market value of $92 billion against a taxable value of $60 billion. The gap between those totals reflects exemptions and assessment caps. The page also lists a homestead filing deadline of March 1, 2027, and says March 2 through December 31 is a pre-filing window for the coming year.

The same page says voters approved a constitutional amendment on November 3, 2026 that affects Florida's property tax system. Call the office to learn how it applies to your parcel before you plan a sale around it.

How are Sanford property taxes and transfer taxes handled at a sale?

Deeds carry 70 cents per hundred dollars of price, with a mortgage counted in the base (s. 201.02). Collection happens at recording, and each party on the deed carries liability (Revenue's stamp tax page).

Tax bills go out in November, discounted from 4 percent that month down to 1 percent in February, and anything unpaid after March 31 is delinquent (taxpayer guide). The appraiser's page also holds parcel splits, combinations and plat recordings until 2026 taxes are paid, which matters if you plan to divide a lot first.

Ask the Seminole County Tax Collector for the balance on your parcel before closing; any unpaid amount comes out of proceeds. The appraiser's page links the collector for in-person, mail and online payment.

After the sale the assessment resets to just value, so a Sanford buyer's bill will differ from yours.

What if the Sanford house is inherited, rented or behind on payments?

  • Inherited house: an estate under $150,000 outside exempt property, or an owner gone over two years, can use summary administration (s. 735.201). Creditors' claims close three months after first notice or 30 days after service, whichever is later (s. 733.702).
  • Rented house: weekly tenancies end on 7 days' notice, monthly on 30 (s. 83.57).
  • Payments behind: following judgment, the clerk sells the house at least 20 and at most 35 days on unless the plaintiff agrees to wait (s. 45.031).

The Seminole County Clerk offers free property fraud alerts, which the appraiser recommends, especially for an empty inherited house.

How does a Sanford house sale close, step by step?

A closing moves from contract to recorded deed in a few steps, and a cash sale drops the lender and appraisal steps. Your title agent or closing attorney coordinates most of it.

  1. Contract: price, closing date, and who pays deed tax and recording.
  2. Title search: surfaces mortgages, judgments and liens, which get paid from proceeds.
  3. Signing: land conveyances need two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01), and witnessing can happen by audio-video technology.
  4. Recording: the closing agent sends the deed to the Seminole County clerk.
  5. Owner update: the appraiser changes the parcel owner after the recorded deed is processed.

The appraiser warns that deed linking can lag when the clerk's records system is down, so an unchanged owner name online right after recording is no cause for alarm.

What else does the property appraiser offer sellers?

The appraiser's site offers parcel and deed searches, plus free downloads of its data in Excel, Access and several GIS formats, updated daily. Exemption or fraud questions go to 407-665-7512. Custom data requests take 10 business days and may carry fees.

New owners are pointed to a First-Time Florida Homebuyer Guide and the Department of Revenue's guide to the property tax system, which a seller can hand to a buyer. Sellers who already hold a homestead should confirm what the office shows on file, since a stale exemption can confuse a closing statement.

  • Check the owner name and mailing address on the parcel record.
  • Confirm the exemption listed matches how you actually use the house.
  • Sign up for fraud alerts through the clerk's office.

More questions about Sanford, FL

Where do I get a parcel record for my Sanford house?

From the Seminole County Property Appraiser, which has an office at 1101 E. 1st Street in Sanford and posts parcel data online. Customer service is 407-665-7506.

Is Sanford in a county with a special stamp tax rate?

No. The 70 cents per $100 deed rate applies in Seminole County, as in every Florida county except Miami-Dade.

Can a house in an older Sanford neighborhood sell as-is?

Yes. Cash buyers regularly buy older houses as-is, and a financed buyer will rely on an inspection and appraisal instead.

When do I have to file for homestead on a new Sanford house?

By March 1, with the county appraiser. That office also accepts pre-filing from March 2 through December 31 for the following year.

What happens to my taxes after I sell?

The assessment resets to just value the next January 1 under the Save Our Homes change-of-ownership rule, so the buyer's bill may differ from yours.

Selling a house in Port Orange FAQ

How much is a house worth in Port Orange?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Port Orange at $287,900.

What sets Port Orange apart for a seller on Florida's Volusia coast?

Port Orange is a Volusia County city along the Halifax River, home to an estimated 66,395 people in July 2025 according to the Census Bureau. The city's history page cites 29 square miles, and the Census lists 26.79 square miles of land.

Volusia County itself spans 1,207 square miles with 47 miles of Atlantic beaches, and its own fast-facts page names Port Orange as the headquarters of a simulation-training developer. Many sellers here are long-time owners, downsizers or heirs, and they usually weigh three routes.

  • An agent listing suits a move-in-ready house when time allows for a buyer's lender.
  • A by-owner sale suits someone at ease with pricing, disclosures and contracts.
  • A cash sale suits a house with deferred work, a probate timeline or a hard deadline.

How does Port Orange's past show up in its streets and neighborhoods?

The city's own history page starts with Timucuan and Seminole peoples, then the 1768 New Smyrna colony and a 995-acre grant to Patrick Dean in 1804 that became the Dunlawton Plantation. The Dunlawton sugar mill on Old Sugar Mill Road still stands after Seminole forces destroyed it twice in 1836.

After the Civil War, Dr. John Milton Hawks and other Union officers brought 500 freed people to land along the Halifax River in 1866. Hawks moved the settlement, first called Orange Port, to its present site in February 1867, and the name became Port Orange by April. The community around Orange Avenue and Charles Street was known informally as Freemanville, and Mount Moriah Baptist Church, built in 1911, remains there.

The area later lived on citrus, lumber, boat building, oystering, ranching and farming. The city says gated communities and growing commercial areas now sit over those older roots.

What is the Port Orange Town Center, and why might it matter to a home near it?

The Town Center is a 271-acre redevelopment district of 300 parcels in eastern Port Orange, created on December 15, 1998. The city says it was historically the commercial core, and the plan pushes mixed-use development and public access to the water.

Five Special Character Districts make up the area: Riverwalk, Causeway, Down Under, Dunlawton Village and Ridgewood Avenue. Funding comes from tax increment financing, which reinvests new property tax revenue above a base level in the district for a set period.

If your house lies in or near these districts, ask the city's planning office for the adopted redevelopment plan, which describes what the city hopes to see built nearby. Buyers who prize riverfront access or walkable errands will ask the same thing.

What do Census figures show for Port Orange?

They show a settled, older, owner-heavy city, with 88.0 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier, 25.2 percent aged 65 or older and commutes of about 25.9 minutes.

Which Volusia landmarks and employers do Port Orange buyers mention?

Buyers often value a short drive to the county's wider draws. Volusia's own fast-facts page highlights Daytona International Speedway and the Daytona 500, Jackie Robinson Ballpark, and DeLand as the county seat with its antique shops and historic downtown. It also lists Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, Stetson University, Bethune-Cookman University, Daytona State College and the University of Central Florida among local institutions.

The county says it sits about an hour north of Disney World and the Kennedy Space Center, so a Port Orange address suits people who commute or travel for work. When you describe your house to a buyer, mention distance to Dunlawton Avenue, the river and the beaches, since those are the references local buyers use.

What do Volusia exemptions and Amendment 3 mean for a Port Orange sale?

The Volusia County Property Appraiser prints the 2026 homestead exemption as up to $51,411, made of $25,000 for all millages plus $26,411 for non-school millages. The same office reports that voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026.

The amendment sets the non-school exemption at up to $150,000 from January 1, 2027 and up to $250,000 from January 1, 2028. School taxes keep the $25,000 limit, and the non-homestead assessment cap drops from 10 percent to 5 percent. Newcomers who become Florida residents on or after January 1, 2027 start at $50,000 and reach the larger amount after four years.

Because Florida resets a property to just value after a sale, a buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours. Ask Volusia's appraiser how your parcel is treated, since implementing legislation may refine details.

  • Cancel your exemption if you move out before March 1.
  • Expect the next owner to file their own.
  • Keep your TRIM notice, which lists exemptions and any capped value.

What utility steps should a Port Orange owner handle with a sale or a tenant?

Port Orange's utilities office says the owner is liable for charges on a property unless the account is formally in a tenant's name. It adds that each time a renter leaves, water service reverts to the owner and is turned off, and each request to start or stop water carries a $40 service fee.

The same page says owners pay monthly water availability fees between renters and that a deposit must be on hold for the account. Leases must be signed and witnessed, and a management agreement is required when an agent handles the rental.

If you are selling a rented house, line these up before closing.

  • Confirm whose name is on the water account and settle any final balance.
  • Send the tenant's lease and any management agreement to the buyer's title agent.
  • Remember that Florida law bars cutting utilities to a tenant without legal authority, which the city cites as section 83.67.

How do heirs and recording work for a Port Orange house?

Summary administration under section 735.201 is open when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner died over two years ago. Creditor claims are barred after the later of three months from first publication or 30 days from service on a creditor who must be served.

The revenue department lists a personal representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable for stamps, but a quit claim deed is. Other deeds carry 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade, collected by the clerk at recording, with all parties liable.

Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and the deed needs two witnesses under section 689.01.

More questions about Port Orange, FL

Is a cash sale a fit for a Port Orange house needing repairs?

It can be. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands and avoids lender appraisals, though title must still be clear.

When did voters approve the new homestead amendment?

The Volusia County Property Appraiser says Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, effective January 1, 2027.

Does a buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?

No. A sale resets the property to just value on the next January 1, per the Department of Revenue, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses.

Can heirs sell before probate ends?

Only with authority to sign. A personal representative or court order usually decides who can convey, so ask the Volusia clerk and an attorney.

What happens to my city water account when I sell?

Port Orange says the owner answers for charges unless the account is in a tenant's name, and a $40 fee applies to each start or stop request. Contact the utilities office before closing.

Selling a house in Apopka FAQ

How much is a house worth in Apopka?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Apopka at $364,300.

Which selling choices does an Apopka owner have?

Apopka owners weigh three paths: an agent, a solo sale, or a buyer paying cash for the house untouched. Each path trades time, effort and net proceeds differently.

Listing works for a tidy house when weeks of showings are fine. Cash works when repairs are looming, an estate is involved, or a renter lives there. All three end at the Orange County recording desk.

  • With an agent: showings and lender timing set the pace.
  • By yourself: you set the price and hire the title company.
  • To a cash buyer: both sides agree the closing day.

Why does Apopka's history and setting matter to a seller?

Apopka sits about twelve miles from Orlando in northwest Orange County, and the city's own profile ranks it behind only Orlando in the county. That profile, written for the 2022-2023 fiscal year, lists a population of 56,727 and an area of 35.512 square miles.

The city dates to the 1840s, when the first settlers arrived, and citizens adopted a charter in 1882 that set the limits at one mile in every direction from the Masonic Lodge on Main Street. Fern growing began in 1922 and made Apopka known as the Fern City, later the Indoor Foliage Capital of the World.

Natural areas are a selling point you can mention in a listing. Wekiva Springs State Park lies about three miles northeast of town, and Rock Springs (Kelly Park) is about six miles north, together roughly 40,000 acres of protected land according to the city.

Who buys homes in Apopka, and how far do they commute?

Many buyers here drive to jobs elsewhere in the Orlando area. The profile gives a median age of 38 and household income at $69,343 and a bachelor's degree held by 30.4 percent of residents.

It also estimates that only 21 percent of residents both live and work in Apopka, with the average commute at 31.6 minutes. So road access toward Orlando may weigh on buyers more than the downtown address; describe the drive when you talk to buyers. The city runs under a mayor-council form of government with a five member council, so permit and code questions about the house go to city staff rather than the county if the address is inside the limits.

What happens to the Orange County tax picture once an Apopka house sells?

Two Orange County offices matter: the appraiser who values the parcel and the tax collector who bills it. Values are fixed each January 1, and a change of ownership puts a homestead back at full market value the next January, so a buyer's bill can run above yours.

The county appraiser's site has a tax estimator that it says helps people planning to buy or sell, and its property search shows sales and foreclosure records by address. Check both you name a price; buyers can pull the same record.

  • Homestead relief reaches $50,000 of value and requires an application to the appraiser by March 1.
  • Save Our Homes holds a homestead's yearly assessment rise to inflation with a 3 percent ceiling; the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A property without homestead can rise at most 10 percent in assessed value per year.
  • November bills carry a 4 percent early discount that shrinks monthly to 1 percent in February, and anything unpaid goes delinquent on April 1.

Have the title company explain how this year's taxes are divided with the buyer, and read that line before agreeing.

How does recording work at the Orange County Comptroller?

The Comptroller's price list starts at $10 for a deed's opening page, then $8.50 per extra page, with $1 for every name past the fourth. Florida adds deed tax of 70 cents on each $100 of price, outside Miami-Dade.

State rules make all parties to the document liable for that tax, whichever one agrees to pay it, and it is paid at recording. A deed sent by post usually waits 7 to 10 business days, e-recording is usually finished within 24 hours, and the quickest option is walking a deed into the office at 109 East Church Street.

Two details trip up sellers. A deed without two subscribing witnesses may not be recognized by the property appraiser for tracking ownership changes, citing section 689.01. And the comptroller cannot give legal advice or supply deed forms, so ask a Florida attorney or your title company to prepare the deed. After closing, your lender's satisfaction of mortgage gets recorded in the same Official Records, and you can search a name there to see liens and judgments. The comptroller will not issue a letter saying a property has no liens.

What happens if the Apopka house is in foreclosure or came from an estate?

Foreclosure and estates both run on statute clocks, and a private sale is still possible if you move early. After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk auctions the property 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to wait, and the top bidder leaves 5 percent down.

For an inherited Apopka house, the Orange County probate papers are not viewable online, since Florida law keeps those document images off the comptroller's website. A short-form summary process exists for estates up to $150,000 and for owners dead more than two years. The revenue department's non-taxable list includes deeds from a court-appointed representative.

What if a renter lives in the Apopka house?

A landlord who is owed rent serves a written notice giving three days, not counting weekends and court holidays. A tenancy running by the month ends on 30 days of notice, and one running by the year needs 60.

Some cash buyers will take a house with a renter inside; read the lease and ask a Florida attorney how it affects the sale. A tenant who contests the case on grounds other than payment has 5 days to deposit the rent with the court. After a judgment, the sheriff posts a 24 hour notice.

What are the practical steps to sell an Apopka house?

  • Look up the parcel and its tax estimate on the county appraiser's site.
  • Gather the deed, mortgage payoff figure, HOA details and any open permits from the city.
  • Compare what you would net from an agent, a solo sale and a cash buyer once taxes and recording charges come out.
  • Choose a title company and ask for the closing statement ahead of time.
  • File the deed at the Orange County Comptroller and send the appraiser your new mailing address.

More questions about Apopka, FL

Who pays doc stamps on an Apopka deed?

Whichever side the contract names, though the state can pursue any party to the deed. The rate outside Miami-Dade is 70 cents on each $100 of price.

When does Orange County reassess a house after I sell it?

The next January 1. A change of ownership resets a homestead to market value as of that date, and the new owner has until March 1 to file for homestead.

How fast will Orange County record my deed?

Between 7 and 10 business days by mail, according to the Comptroller. E-recording is usually done within 24 hours, and walking it in is the fastest way.

Can I sell an Apopka house I inherited without probate?

Not always. Where the estate is small enough or the owner died over two years ago, summary administration is available, and a personal representative's deed is not subject to doc stamp tax. Ask a Florida attorney which path fits.

What do I owe if the property taxes are unpaid at closing?

Get a balance from the Orange County Tax Collector before closing. After April 1 an unpaid bill is delinquent, and certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1.

Selling a house in Palm Beach Gardens FAQ

How much is a house worth in Palm Beach Gardens?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Palm Beach Gardens at $554,300.

How fast can a Palm Beach Gardens house sell?

As fast as the buyer's financing and your repair list allow. A cash purchase can close on a date you pick, and a full listing may fetch more but brings showings and inspections.

Palm Beach Gardens is a high-value market, so the tax, permit and recording details deserve more attention here than in many Florida cities. The sections below cover the city's planned origins, its numbers and the rules a seller meets.

How was Palm Beach Gardens built?

It began as a planned community. On March 20, 1959, John D. MacArthur announced plans to develop about 4,000 acres for 55,000 people, according to the city's About page.

His preferred name, Palm Beach city, was refused, so he chose Palm Beach Gardens to fit his garden city plan. He had streets and construction routed around mature trees such as the banyans, and churches went up first. By 1964 he had attracted the Professional Golfers Association, whose clubhouse opened in March 1965, and the PGA left in 1972. In 1999 the MacArthur Foundation sold about 14,000 acres, around 5,000 of them in the city.

For a seller, this history explains the mature tree cover, the waterways and the master-planned layout many buyers see on the streets.

How do Palm Beach Gardens statistics look?

Home values sit well above most of the state and the population skews older, as the city-wide figures below show.

Palm Beach Gardens, by the numbersReported value

Which city rules affect a Palm Beach Gardens seller?

The city's FAQ page covers several items that buyers' inspectors and title agents raise.

  • Permits: roof replacement, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, window and door replacement and additions all need a permit, filed through the online permitting system with items such as plans, contractor details and a survey.
  • Owner-builders: homeowners may pull certain permits themselves with an Owner-Builder Affidavit but take full responsibility for the work and code compliance.
  • Trees: a Certified Arborist is on staff, tree removal falls under Section 78-328 of the city code, and a dead tree, palm or shrub should be replaced within one month.
  • Plants: Brazilian pepper, Australian pine and melaleuca are prohibited, and plant beds need three inches of mulch.
  • Violations: after notice, an owner who does not correct a violation can be sent to the Special Magistrate, with fines and liens possible.

The city also runs a Single-Family Home Improvement Grant for owner-occupied, homesteaded houses within city limits, with income capped at 120 percent of area median income and liquid assets capped at $50,000. It funds exterior hardening, energy and accessibility work such as roofs, windows and doors.

Two more local notes. Palm Beach Gardens follows the South Florida Water Management District's watering schedule for Palm Beach County, and the city says its authority to regulate the siting and occupancy of group and community residential homes is limited by Florida Statute 419, the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Fair Housing Act. City Council meetings are held on the first Thursday of each month unless noted. The Planning and Zoning page tells you to check the property appraiser's municipality field to confirm a lot lies inside city limits.

Landscaping can affect both curb appeal and compliance here. The city's forestry answers say 'all types of organic mulch are allowed' and that xeriscape, which reduces irrigation needs, is encouraged, and it advises trimming dead branches before hurricane season. Walk the lot before photos so no prohibited plants or dead trees show up in a buyer's inspection.

Does age change how a Palm Beach Gardens owner sells?

It can. With about a third of residents 65 or older, many sellers here are downsizing after decades in the same house, and several Florida benefits are tied to age and service.

  • An ordinance may grant owners 65 and over an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 within a household income limit. Ask the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser whether your address qualifies.
  • A veteran aged 65 or over with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability rating.
  • A tax deferral application goes to the tax collector by March 31, and a permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent of household income.
  • Homestead ends once the home is rented or stops being your permanent residence.

If you are moving within Florida, portability can carry up to $500,000 of cap savings to the new homestead, according to the statute. Amendments from chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 tax roll.

How do taxes and fees work when a house sells here?

The property appraiser values the house each January 1, and the tax collector bills in November. Unpaid bills go delinquent on April 1, and certificates are sold by June 1.

Stamps on a Palm Beach County deed run $0.70 for each $100 of price. Clerk recording charges are added, opening at $5.00 on page one, with smaller trust fund and technology charges added per page. Your title agent can total this early, so the figure is known before you sign.

  • To dispute a value, file a petition inside 25 days after the August notice of proposed taxes.
  • If an exemption is denied, petition the value adjustment board inside 30 days after the denial letter is mailed.

Also keep in mind that Florida does not tax the estate of someone who died after 2004, so heirs selling a Palm Beach Gardens house face deed stamps and closing costs but no state estate tax return.

What if a lender, a tax lien or an unwanted occupant is involved?

A judicial foreclosure sale takes place at least 20 days after final judgment and no more than 35 unless the plaintiff agrees to wait. The high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale. A homestead owner should ask the clerk about surplus funds during the 10 days that follow the sale.

Tax certificates run on a separate track, and a holder may seek a tax deed after two years. For a person occupying a home with no right to be there, Florida lets an owner file a verified complaint with the sheriff, but false statements expose the owner to triple the fair market rent plus fees. If the person is a tenant, use the notice process instead. Check on vacant seasonal or inherited houses often.

More questions about Palm Beach Gardens, FL

Which county appraises Palm Beach Gardens homes?

Palm Beach County. The county property appraiser values the house and the county tax collector bills it. The city's own site links to the appraiser to verify where you live.

How old is the city?

Its founding announcement came on March 20, 1959, when John D. MacArthur announced plans for about 4,000 acres. It is a planned community, not a historic town.

How much are deed stamps in this county?

$0.70 per $100 of price, the standard Florida rate. Only Miami-Dade differs.

Can a senior defer property tax?

Possibly. File form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31. A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the portion above 3 percent of household income.

Later arrivals from France, Spain and England also relied on the waterways. In the mid-1800s the federal government built the Jupiter Lighthouse, and the settlement around it grew into the town.

From the mid-1800s into the early 1900s the Inlet Village area worked as a fishing village and a port. A long wharf moved goods onto the Celestial Railroad, which ran between Jupiter and Juno Beach. St. Martin's Episcopal Church was built there in 1899, and guests from the north came to stay at vacation homes and to hire fishing guides on the river. Developers eyed the area in the 1920s, but the Great Depression stopped their plans, and trade shifted to U.S. 1 and the Florida East Coast Railroad. What does Florida charge to transfer a deed in Winter Haven?

The deed tax statute names a rate of 70 cents per $100 of price, and Florida's revenue agency says every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay. The clerk collects it when the deed is filed. Section 28.24(13) fixes a base of $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each later page, before trust fund and technology add-ons. Start with the code compliance office, because its published answers cover parking, right-of-way upkeep and rentals. Its FAQ says violation notices go to the property owner, not the tenant, so an open violation on your address is your problem to clear before closing.

Rentals are tightly limited. The city's FAQ states that advertising a rental for less than three months is prohibited, and that renting for three months or less, or renting more than four times in a twelve month period, is prohibited. If your house has been used for short stays, buyers will raise it, so stop any short stays before you list.

  • Ask code compliance whether the address has open violations or an unfinished inspection.
  • Keep the right-of-way in front of the lot maintained, since owners are responsible for it.
  • Do not divide a single-family home into units without permits from the city's Building Department.
  • Ask whether a certificate of use or business tax receipt is attached to the property.

The city's code compliance phone line is listed on its site, and calling it before you list is cheaper than learning about a problem from the buyer's title company.

How much does a North Miami closing cost in taxes and fees?

Deed stamp tax is the largest state item, and Miami-Dade sets its own schedule. The state's revenue department prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, with the surtax left off a document that conveys only a single-family dwelling. Elsewhere in Florida the rate is 70 cents.

Closing items on a North Miami deed, from official Florida pages
ItemWhat the official page says
Deed stamp tax, Miami-Dade60 cents per $100, plus 45 cents per $100 surtax (not due on a single-family dwelling only)
Liability for the taxAll parties to the document are liable
Clerk recording, first page$5.00
Clerk recording, each added page$4.00
Collected byCounty clerk, at recording

The statute also lists small extra charges per page, so the title company's settlement statement is the place to see the final recording total. Mortgage payoffs, association fees and prorated property tax come out of your proceeds at closing.

How does the county tax bill figure into my sale?

Each January 1 fixes the assessed value, and the tax collector sends bills in November. The Miami-Dade appraiser's homestead page sets March 1 as the application deadline and accepts late filings until the cutoff shown on the proposed tax notice, usually 25 days after mailing. It adds that renewal receipts do not go to properties with a change of ownership, deeds by warranty or quitclaim included.

An exemption follows the person, not the house. The buyer files fresh, and the sale resets the assessed figure to market level the next January 1.

What does Florida's Amendment 3 change for North Miami homeowners?

The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser's page says Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and that it takes effect January 1, 2027, first applying to the 2027 tax year. It raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028 for owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026. From 2029 the amount is adjusted for positive consumer price index changes, and the school board portion stays at $25,000.

Newcomers are treated differently. Someone who becomes a Florida resident after the start of 2027 may start with up to $50,000 against non-school taxes, and generally reaches the higher amount in the fifth year of holding a homestead. The appraiser notes that the five-year rule is subject to federal constitutional limits and to implementing legislation.

For a seller the lesson is plain. Do not quote a buyer's future tax bill in a listing. Point buyers to the appraiser, whose phone number appears on the homestead page, and let them confirm what applies to them.

What about an inherited or tenant occupied house?

Yes to both, with conditions. An inherited house needs someone with authority to sign, so the title company will ask for probate letters or proof the property passed outside probate. The state's list shows a personal representative's deed under a probated will as one that owes no stamp tax.

With a tenant, hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. Some cash buyers accept the tenant and others want the unit empty at closing. North Miami limits short rentals, so confirm any short-stay use was lawful before you describe it.

Moving the house to a relative first can add cost, since quitclaim deeds are on the taxable list and may change how the county treats ownership.

What is a sensible timeline for a sale?

With clean title a cash sale can wrap up in a couple of weeks. A financed sale runs longer because of the appraisal and loan approval. Allow time for payoff letters, an association estoppel and clearing any permit or violation.

  • First week: gather the deed, tax bill, payoff and association papers.
  • Next: pick an offer and a closing date.
  • Then: title search, lien and violation clearing, signing appointment.
  • Closing: signing before witnesses or a notary, then recording.

A contract with a firm date and a plain list of seller repairs prevents the most common slips.

More questions about North Miami, FL

What is the stamp tax rate on a deed in North Miami?

Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, per the state revenue department, and the surtax is not due when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Your title company can give the figure for your deed.

Can I rent the house short term while it is listed?

The city's published answer says rentals of three months or less are prohibited, as is renting more than four times in twelve months. Check with code compliance before any short stay.

Does the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?

No. The buyer applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the sale resets assessed value to market level the next January 1.

Who is responsible for a code violation notice at my address?

The city addresses the notice to the owner. A tenant should speak with the landlord, but plan to clear the violation before closing.

What is Amendment 3 and when does it start?

The county appraiser reports that voters approved it on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year, raising the non-school homestead exemption for eligible owners.

Selling a house in Margate FAQ

How much is a house worth in Margate?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Margate at $286,200.

How would you describe Margate's setting?

Margate is in Broward County and was created as the Town of Margate on May 30, 1955, then took city status in 1961. The city's area page puts it at about nine square miles with 30 miles of canals, 7.5 miles from the Atlantic and roughly 20 minutes from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport and Port Everglades.

The name is said to come from the founder's surname and the word gateway, because the town was seen as a gateway to western Broward. The city provides its own police, fire and emergency medical services, water, wastewater and stormwater service, and it counts 19 parks and recreational facilities including the Calypso Cove aquatics site. Northwest Medical Center and the city itself are among the major employers listed.

Its Community Redevelopment Agency dates to 1996. The same page reports a median age of 46.4 and 2.48 people per household, using older figures, so treat them as background and not as a market reading.

  • Margate runs its own water and sewer, so request a final meter reading from the city at closing.
  • Canal frontage and distance to the coast are worth stating in a listing.
  • A buyer from outside Florida may ask about insurance, so gather your policy details.

Can I still sell a Margate house after a foreclosure suit starts?

You can sell before a court sale takes the house, and Florida's process often leaves a wider window than owners expect. The lender sues in Broward County, wins a final judgment, and only then does the clerk schedule an auction.

Once judgment is entered, the sale date must land 35 days out at the latest and 20 days out at the earliest, absent the lender's consent to a later date (s. 45.031). Notice is published for two consecutive weeks, the top bidder leaves a deposit, and an objection period of 10 days follows the certificate of sale. Under s. 702.10 a lender can seek a faster order to show cause, but a granted homestead exemption on the latest roll creates a presumption of owner occupancy, which keeps a Margate homeowner on the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

What happens to extra money if a Margate house sells at auction?

Whatever remains after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The judgment carries a notice about it, and homestead owners are told to check in within 10 days.

Claims have to be filed before the clerk reports the money as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your terms usually leaves more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and hands you the balance.

Which months carry a Margate tax discount?

Bills arrive in November, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Paying early earns a sliding discount.

Early-payment discounts on a Broward tax bill
Month paidDiscount
November4 percent

February1 percent

Relief exists for owners who are short of cash. A homestead owner short of the full amount can file Form DR-570 for deferral by the March 31 after the assessment year, covering the part above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

How do tax certificates and tax deeds threaten a Margate owner who stops paying?

Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate, sold by June 1 to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest, in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The certificate holder is barred from pressing the owner for payment during the first two years, counted from April 1 of the year of issue.

After that, a tax deed application can be filed for a $75 fee (s. 197.502). The clerk runs the auction, and on homestead land the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value. Before listing, ask the Broward tax collector whether any certificate is attached to the parcel.

What should I gather before talking to a Margate buyer?

Collect the papers that answer a buyer's first questions, so the offer reflects the real condition of the house. Missing papers are a common cause of a late closing.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • Your newest tax bill, plus a note of any certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

Florida requires a land transfer to be written and signed in front of two witnesses, and witnessing may happen by audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Plan signing early when an owner lives out of state. For exemption questions, the Broward County Property Appraiser lists 954-357-6830, open weekdays.

Which offers suit a Margate owner in a hurry?

A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and repairs become the buyer's job.

Get the closing date, the payoff and each fee on paper first. Ask whether the deposit can be refunded, who picks the title company, and how a request for more time would be handled. Sellers who compare two or three written offers, with the same lines filled in, tend to spot the weak ones fast.

If you plan to stay a few weeks after closing, ask for a short rent-back in writing, with a daily rate and a move-out date. Take photos of the house at handover so both sides agree on its condition.

Which Margate services might matter to a buyer or an older seller?

The city area page describes two special districts tied to the commission: the Northwest Focal Point Senior Center, which serves adults age 60 and older in the city and county, and the Community Redevelopment Agency created in 1996. Programs listed for seniors include transportation, an eldercare advocate, home energy assistance and meals.

An older owner who is selling to move closer to family can ask the center about the help on offer before the move. Buyers who are retirees may ask about those services, and the city also points to a fire department rated ISO Class I and recognition for its police department. Cite those points only as the city states them, and let a buyer check the details.

Median household income and age figures on the page are older estimates, so do not quote them as current. Stick to facts you can confirm with the city and keep the listing description plain, so that a buyer's own research matches what you wrote.

More questions about Margate, FL

What is the gap between foreclosure judgment and auction?

The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031).

Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?

Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?

No. A deed application cannot be filed until two years have run from April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what clearing it would cost.

How does the Florida tax deferral work?

The owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector, deferring the part above 5 percent of last year's household income.

Who provides water and sewer in Margate?

The city's area page lists water, wastewater and stormwater among its own services, so a closing should include a final utility reading.

How much is a house worth in Coconut Creek?

What kind of housing market is Coconut Creek in Broward County?

Coconut Creek is a Broward County city with 58,626 residents on the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, up from 52,909 in 2010 and 57,833 in 2020. It is compact: 11.17 square miles of land held roughly 5,179 residents per square mile when the 2020 Census was taken. Check whether your home belongs to a homeowner or condominium association, since the vacation rental affidavit on the city's site refers to notice to a mandatory association and its rules can add steps to a sale.

What housing figures does the Census report for Coconut Creek?

A typical owner-occupied Coconut Creek home was valued at $309,600 for 2020 through 2024, and 64.8% of housing is lived in by its owner. Rent at the midpoint is $2,102 a month, so owners of rental units can compare that income with what a sale would bring.

Does Coconut Creek allow vacation rentals, and does that matter for a sale?

Yes. The city's vacation rental page says its regulations do not prohibit vacation rentals or limit how long or how often a home is rented. They exist to protect neighborhoods and life safety, and every vacation rental must register and obtain a Vacation Rental Certification.

If you hold one, tell buyers up front. A certification is part of the property's income story, and a buyer who wants it has to file a new application. The city lists these details:

The city page also gives a notarized-letter option for owners whose booking sites collect taxes. Ask the city's business tax office for the current form.

What should a Coconut Creek landlord do before selling a rented house?

Read the lease first. Florida needs at least 30 days of notice to end a tenancy that renews monthly, and a tenant behind on rent is owed 3 days of written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays. Florida's eviction statute lays out the notice and the court steps, so follow them if a tenant must leave before closing.

Selling with the tenant staying means the rent keeps flowing and no gap opens between occupants. Put the lease, security deposit amount and rent ledger in the contract package.

How does Broward treat deed tax on a Coconut Creek sale?

In Broward the deed tax is the statewide 70 cents per $100 of price. Only Miami-Dade differs. The tax covers any mortgage or encumbrance on the property whether or not the buyer takes it over, every person on the deed answers for it regardless of what the contract says, and the Broward clerk collects it at recording.

Statutory recording charges are separate: a first page costs $5.00 and later pages are $4.00 apiece, plus other per-page fees. Have the closing agent list each one.

How do Broward homestead and property tax dates affect a Coconut Creek sale?

The first $25,000 reaches every tax; the second $25,000 applies only above $50,000 of value and only to non-school taxes.

Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower. The sale itself resets the parcel to just value on the following January 1. Bills arrive each November with discounts that shrink from 4 percent to 1 percent by February, and April 1 is the delinquency date. A mid-year closing means the title company divides the tax with the buyer.

What if a Coconut Creek owner faces foreclosure or an inherited house?

Foreclosure here is a court matter. The clerk holds the auction within a window of 20 to 35 days after final judgment, longer if the lender consents. If the house sells first, the lender is paid from the proceeds. If the house came from an estate, a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less can use summary administration, as can an estate where more than two years have gone by since the death.

Either case rewards an early call to the servicer, a Florida attorney or the probate clerk. A cash buyer can work around those dates, yet the court sets the schedule.

What if property taxes on a Coconut Creek house go unpaid?

Delinquency starts April 1. The tax collector then sells certificates on the unpaid bills by June 1, and bidders offer the lowest interest rate they will accept, in quarter-point steps. The certificate holder may not ask the owner for money until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

Once two years pass, the holder can request a tax deed for a $75 application fee, and the clerk conducts the auction. A homestead's opening bid includes half of its assessed value. Back taxes can be cleared from proceeds at closing; request the payoff figure from the title company.

Which Florida tax breaks might apply to a Coconut Creek owner?

Owners 65 or older may get another homestead exemption of up to $50,000 where a local ordinance allows it and household income stays under the limit. A 10 percent or greater disability, with an honorable discharge and Florida residency, brings a $5,000 cut in assessed value. Total and permanent service-connected disability can qualify for a full homestead exemption. The Census counts 1,850 veterans in Coconut Creek, so these rules reach real owners here.

Homestead ends when you rent the home or move out, though a servicemember may rent without losing it. Ask the Broward property appraiser which exemptions sit on your parcel before closing.

More questions about Coconut Creek, FL

Can I sell a Coconut Creek house that has a vacation rental certification?

Yes. The certification belongs to the current owner, and a buyer planning short-term stays has to register separately. Check the city's annual September 30 renewal date and your fee status before closing.

Do I owe the city anything before I sell my Coconut Creek home?

Ask the city's Building Division about open permits and the code office about open violations, since either can hold up closing.

HOA approval, title work and any lien payoffs can still add days.

The lease generally carries on unless it ends or the proper notice is served. Florida requires at least 30 days of notice for a tenant renewing monthly.

Selling a house in Sarasota FAQ

How much is a house worth in Sarasota?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Sarasota at $409,700.

Which route sells a Sarasota house fastest?

Cash is quickest for a Sarasota house because it skips lender approval, an appraisal and most repair haggling. Listing takes longer and reaches more buyers, which can raise the price.

Houses here are judged on bay access, flood and wind exposure, and age. Owners who want a fast exit usually hold an inherited property, a house with deferred repairs, or a rental with someone living in it. Each is handled differently, and the sections below point to the Sarasota and Florida pages that govern them.

  • Cash purchase: quickest close, bought as-is, negotiated figure.
  • Agent listing: more preparation, broader market.
  • Private sale: you manage the contract and closing paperwork.

How did Sarasota's neighborhoods come about?

The city's own history pages describe Sarasota's early growth through its plats. Newtown, near downtown, began on April 20, 1914, when the original Newtown plat was filed with Manatee County with 96 building lots. A first addition filed on August 6, 1914 added 74 more.

The city notes that Newtown grew out of Overtown, the first enclave established by African American residents in Sarasota, and that Black labor cleared land for developers, laid railroad ties, harvested celery and platted golf courses over more than a century. The city also hosts a Newtown history site and a timeline for visitors.

Platted history matters when you sell, because the lot lines, easements and setbacks on an older plat decide what a buyer can build or add. If you have an old survey, keep it with the sale papers. If not, a title agent can tell you what the recorded plat shows for your lot.

What does the Sarasota County Property Appraiser publish each year?

The office is at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota, phone 941.861.8200, and posts notices tied to the annual cycle. Its home page shows the 2026 sequence, which follows the statewide calendar.

Sarasota County 2026 assessment notices as posted by the property appraiser
NoticeDate posted
2025 rolls recertified to the tax collectorMay 21, 2026
2026 TRIM notices mailedAugust 17, 2026
2026 rolls certified to the tax collectorSeptember 29, 2026

Source: Sarasota County Property Appraiser.

The same page offers a copy of each TRIM notice through the property search and links to Hurricane Evacuation Levels, a useful reference when a buyer asks about storm risk at your address. It also recommends the Clerk's free fraud alert, which emails you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name.

How do Florida property tax dates affect a Sarasota sale?

Florida assesses on January 1 and bills in November. Paying that month saves 4 percent, and the discount shrinks to 1 percent by February; unpaid bills go delinquent April 1 and certificates are sold by June 1 (taxpayer guide).

Homestead filings are due March 1. Selling and buying again within Florida lets you port part of a Save Our Homes benefit to the new house, within the filing window (Save Our Homes guide).

A sale resets the parcel to just value on the following January 1, so a Sarasota seller should avoid handing a buyer a tax estimate built from the present bill.

What will the Sarasota deed transfer cost?

Deed stamp tax in Sarasota County is 70 cents per hundred dollars of price, and a loan on the property counts toward that price (s. 201.02). Everyone on the deed answers to the state, though the contract normally assigns payment to one side.

The clerk's recording charge is set by s. 28.24 and itemized on the closing statement. The state also exempts a spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage, plus divorce deeds for the marital home (stamp tax page).

What if a Sarasota house is inherited, tenant-occupied or in default?

  • Inherited: an estate of $150,000 or less outside exempt items, or an owner gone over two years, can use summary administration (s. 735.201). Deaths after 2004 carry no Florida estate tax.
  • Tenant: unpaid rent triggers a three-day notice that skips weekends and court holidays (s. 83.56). A fixable lease breach gets seven days.
  • Default: after judgment the clerk sells 20 to 35 days later, and the top bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit (s. 45.031).

Selling before that auction keeps price and timing in your hands. After it, leftover funds are claimed through the clerk.

How should a Sarasota seller prepare the house and paperwork?

Collect the deed, survey, recent tax bill, permit finals and any insurance claim records. Flood and storm history gets heavy attention in a coastal county, so be ready to answer questions about past water or roof damage.

  1. Order a payoff statement from each lender or lienholder.
  2. Check homestead status with the Sarasota County Property Appraiser.
  3. Sign up for the Clerk's fraud alerts if the house will sit empty.
  4. Ask your title agent which documents the Sarasota County recording office needs.

Those four steps reduce surprises whether you list or take a cash offer.

What do buyers ask about storm risk on a Sarasota house?

Expect buyers and their insurers to ask where the house falls on the county's hurricane evacuation levels, which the property appraiser's home page links under that title. Look up your address before listing so you can answer directly instead of guessing.

Roof age, window protection and past claims usually come next. Permit records for roof and window work help here, and so do the product approvals and installer paperwork that went with those jobs. A house with a documented, permitted roof is easier to insure and easier to price. A house with gaps in its records can still sell, most often to an investor who plans to handle repairs after closing and prices that work into the offer.

  • Pull permit finals for roof, windows and electrical.
  • Gather insurance declarations and any claim letters.
  • Note any past water intrusion and the repair that followed.

Which Sarasota office handles which record?

A sale touches several offices, and calling the wrong one wastes days. In Florida each county elects its own property appraiser, tax collector and clerk of the circuit court, so Sarasota County's offices are separate from the city's departments.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and the TRIM notice, at 2001 Adams Lane.
  • Tax collector: mails the November bill, takes payment and sells tax certificates on unpaid accounts.
  • Clerk: records the deed, collects stamp tax at recording and runs foreclosure and tax deed sales. The clerk's free fraud alert emails you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name.
  • City of Sarasota: planning, historic preservation and building matters inside city limits.

Match the route to your deadline. An agent listing can reach the top price but demands prep and showings; a for-sale-by-owner effort saves a commission and costs time; a direct purchase by a cash company gives up some price for a firm date.

Bradenton lies on the Manatee River in Manatee County, and your paperwork runs through county offices: the Property Appraiser for value and exemptions, the Tax Collector for the bill, and the Clerk for recording. What parts of Bradenton shape buyer interest?

The river and downtown do. The city describes the Bradenton Riverwalk as a 2.03-mile stretch between the Green and DeSoto bridges along the Manatee River, with a lighted path, fishing, a skate park, a playground and a splash pad. Riverwalk stays open around the clock, while other city parks open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Near downtown sits the Village of the Arts, which the city places between 9th Street West and 14th Street West and between 9th Avenue West and 17th Avenue West. Other draws the city lists include LECOM Park, where the Bradenton Marauders have played since 2010, the Herrig Center for the Arts at 888 3rd Ave. W, the Bishop Museum of Science and Nature and River Run Golf Links on the Braden River.

What dates does the Manatee County Property Appraiser follow?

How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Bradenton sale?

A homestead exemption can reach $50,000. The first $25,000 touches every tax; the second $25,000 skips school taxes and applies to assessed value above $50,000. Save Our Homes then restrains yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is smaller.

The buyer does not inherit that cap, since a change of ownership sends the property back to just value the next year. A seller can carry some of the benefit to a new home through portability, up to $500,000 of the gap per the statute, if the new homestead is established inside the three-year window.

Leasing the house ends homestead, so a move-out followed by a rental changes the exemption on the next roll.

When a house closes between November and the following March, the closing agent usually splits the year's bill between seller and buyer. Ask the Manatee County Tax Collector what was billed and whether an early discount applied. Back taxes lead to certificate sales by June 1, so pay them off at closing to keep the title clean.

How do I weigh offers on a Bradenton property?

Compare them on what lands in your account and on how likely each deal is to close. A list price tells you little until you subtract commissions, repairs, carrying costs and the weeks of waiting, and a cash buyer's figure should be read the same way.

  • Count the months you would keep paying the mortgage, insurance and utilities while a listing sits.
  • Price the repairs a lender-backed buyer would demand after an inspection.
  • Ask each buyer for proof of funds or a loan commitment letter.
  • Confirm the closing date and whether you may extend it if you need more time to move.

Two offers at the same price can differ by thousands once those items are counted, so ask a title agent to draft a mock settlement statement for each one before choosing.

Which deed charges hit a Bradenton closing?

Every $100 of consideration on a deed carries 70 cents of stamp tax in Manatee County, a rate that applies everywhere but Miami-Dade. Liability reaches every party named on the document, so the closing agent normally pays at recording.

Recording charges come on top, set per page by section 28.24, and the Clerk of the Circuit Court can quote the figure for your exact document.

  • The tax reaches warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds alike.
  • Deeds given to a lender in place of foreclosure are taxable too.
  • Have the closing agent total both lines before signing day.

May heirs sell an inherited Bradenton home?

Yes, after someone gains court authority to sign for the estate. Section 735.201 allows a shorter process, summary administration, for estates under $150,000 in non-exempt assets or where the owner died over two years ago.

Creditors face a cutoff as well, tied to publication of the notice to creditors or to service on a known creditor. No Florida estate tax applies to anyone who died after December 31, 2004. The state lists a deed from a court-appointed personal representative as not taxable. Consult a probate lawyer before you advertise or sign anything.

What if tenants or a lender are involved?

Ending a monthly tenancy takes at least 30 days of notice before a rental month closes (section 83.57), while unpaid rent calls for a three-day notice that skips weekends and court holidays (section 83.56). Read the lease before telling a buyer the house will be empty, and keep copies of every notice you serve.

If a lender has already sued, a final judgment sets a public sale not less than 20 or more than 35 days after judgment, under section 45.031. The winning bidder posts a deposit, and objections have a short window after the certificate of sale. Anyone facing this should speak with a Florida attorney and the county clerk about surplus funds and timing.

More questions about Bradenton, FL

Where is Bradenton and which county handles my taxes?

Bradenton lies on the Manatee River in Manatee County. The Manatee County Property Appraiser sets value and the Manatee County Tax Collector mails bills in November.

What is the homestead deadline for Manatee County?

March 1 of the year the exemption should apply. The Property Appraiser's date list gives the same deadline for the low-income senior, widow, widower and non-profit exemptions.

Can I appeal my Bradenton property value?

Yes. TRIM notices go out in August and a 25-day appeal period begins at mailing. The exact deadline for the Value Adjustment Board petition is printed on the notice.

Does a sale change the assessed value?

For the buyer, yes. A change of ownership returns the property to just value the following January 1, so the Save Our Homes cap starts over once they claim homestead.

How much time passes before a foreclosure sale?

The clerk sets the sale between 20 and 35 days after final judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer. Confirm dates with your attorney.

  • Cash buyer: accepts the property with its flaws, and the closing day is negotiated.

Whichever route you choose, Lee County's property appraiser, tax collector and clerk all play a part, so start with the property record for your address.

Where did Bonita Springs come from?

Bonita Springs began as a settlement called Survey, named after Army Corps of Engineers surveyors who camped on the upper Imperial River in the 1870s. A post office opened in 1901, the Eagle Hotel was serving hunting and fishing visitors by 1910, and developers later renamed the town to sell it better.

Barron Collier extended his rail line south in the early 1920s, and the Tamiami Trail opened in 1928, bringing a land boom and a brief first incorporation. Roadside attractions followed, with the Everglades Reptile Gardens opening in 1936 and a greyhound track in December 1957. The city says air conditioning, Interstate 75, a nearby major airport and the US 41 bypass drove growth in the 1980s and 1990s, bringing malls, offices and golf courses. Residents voted to incorporate again in 1999.

That layered growth explains why a Bonita Springs street can mix older homes with golf course communities, so the age of your house shapes what a buyer will inspect.

What does Hurricane Ian mean for selling a Bonita Springs house?

If your house was damaged, report it to the Lee County Property Appraiser, because the new value is set as of January 1 following the event and the damage is factored into it. The appraiser's hurricane page asks owners to email hurricaneupdate@leepa.org or use its reporting link.

The page explains that residential owners can apply for a partial tax refund depending on the extent of damage and whether they could use the property, with details in section 197.319 of the Florida Statutes. It adds that a rebuild that changes the property significantly will likely raise its value, while a rebuild similar to the old one should have a minimal effect. Permits are still required under each jurisdiction's process, and the FEMA 50 percent rule applies to substantial repairs, so ask the city's building staff what applies before you spend money on a house you plan to sell.

The appraiser also issues a tax roll value letter for many parcels to help owners apply the FEMA 50 percent rule, which compares repair cost with a structure's value. Vacant land, many commercial properties and condominiums may have no letter. The page says there are deadlines for starting repairs if you want to keep a homestead on a damaged house, so ask the appraiser's exemption staff at exemptions@leepa.org before you decide between repairing and selling.

  • Condominiums do not get a tax roll value letter, because the appraiser does not split land and building value for a whole complex.
  • A private appraisal of the entire complex is the route the appraiser suggests for condo owners working with their association.
  • Do not register to vote or get a driver license elsewhere while repairing, or the homestead exemption could be jeopardized; changing your mailing address is fine.

How do Lee County property taxes work when I sell?

Lee County values each parcel on January 1 and bills in November, and a sale puts the next owner's assessment back at market the January after. Homestead relief of up to $50,000 requires a March 1 application, and Save Our Homes limits yearly growth to inflation or 3 percent, whichever is lower; the state lists 2.7 percent for 2026.

What taxes apply to a Bonita Springs deed?

Lee County deeds carry Florida's deed tax at 70 cents for each $100 of price, and every signer answers to the state for it. The clerk takes payment at recording.

The clerk's recording charges are set by statute and are per page, and the deed needs two subscribing witnesses. The state's list leaves out deeds by a court-appointed representative, and exempts a spouse's homestead deed where a mortgage is the only consideration.

What if the house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?

Each situation runs on a state clock. Small estates, up to $150,000, or those open more than two years after death, can use the summary route.

For a tenant behind on rent, Florida allows a written three day notice that skips weekends and court holidays. A foreclosure sale follows judgment by 20 to 35 days.

When taxes go unpaid, certificates are sold by June 1, and the holder can seek a tax deed two years later. Ask the Lee County Tax Collector for a payoff before you pick a closing day.

What local landmarks and growth shape a Bonita Springs listing?

Bonita Springs has long been inhabited. The city's history page says archaeological finds place people here about 8,000 years ago, with mound building well underway by 4,000 years ago, and the Calusa were in contact with Ponce de Leon in 1513. Today the city describes itself as an affluent area with beaches, restaurants, recreation facilities and attractive homes.

The Everglades Wonder Gardens, which the city calls one of the few remaining historic resources of its roadside type in Florida, is a local landmark from the 1930s. The 1980s and 1990s growth brought shopping malls, modern office buildings and golf courses, so the house you are selling may sit among very different generations of building. Mention its age and any updates plainly, and keep permits and repair records handy for whoever buys it.

What are the steps to close a Bonita Springs sale?

  1. Search the parcel on the Lee County appraiser's site and note exemptions and any damage report.
  2. Request a lender payoff and a tax balance from the tax collector.
  3. Check city permit records for open or unpermitted work.
  4. Weigh each sale route by what you net after taxes and recording charges.
  5. Sign the deed before two witnesses and record it with the Lee County clerk.

Is Bonita Springs in Lee County?

Yes, and the Lee County Property Appraiser values its parcels. Voters made it a city in 1999, after a brief earlier incorporation in the 1920s.

Do I need to tell the appraiser about hurricane damage?

Yes. The appraiser asks owners to report damage because the new value is set as of the January 1 after the event. Residential owners may also apply for a partial refund under section 197.319.

Can I keep my homestead while repairing a storm-damaged house?

Yes, if you tell the appraiser you intend to repair or rebuild and make it your permanent residence. Avoid actions like registering to vote or getting a license in another county or state.

What is the doc stamp rate in Lee County?

Seventy cents for each $100 of price. The state can look to any party on the deed, whoever the contract assigns it to.

What happens to my homestead exemption after I sell?

It leaves with you. The next owner applies by March 1 for their own, and the parcel is reassessed at market the January after the sale.

Why do military and tourism matter to Pensacola home sales?

The stamp tax binds every signer of the deed, so write into the contract which side covers it. Request the full settlement statement several days before closing.

What if my Pensacola house has liens, a foreclosure or an unpaid estate?

A sale can still work. Court-ordered foreclosure sales fall 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer, so a private buyer who moves quickly can pay off the lender first. Estates under $150,000 qualify for summary administration, and creditors have a fixed window to file claims.

Ask a Florida attorney which route your facts fit, and ask the Escambia County clerk how to record the deed once authority is in place.

The land area was 13.63 square miles in 2010 and 18.00 in 2020, so the city boundary itself has expanded along with the headcount.

Is my Clermont mailing address inside the city limits?

Not always. The city tells owners that a Clermont mailing address does not prove a parcel lies within city limits, and it points them to the Lake County Property Appraiser site: search the address, open the Alternate Key, and read the millage group. A plain number marks unincorporated Lake County, while letters such as GR or MI mark Groveland or Minneola.

The answer decides which building department issued your permits, which codes applied and which tax bill you will split at closing. Confirm it first, then gather permits from the right office.

What permit questions arise when a Clermont house goes on the market?

The city's Building Services FAQ says almost everything may need a permit, with exceptions such as replacing kitchen cabinets, flooring and painting. Homeowners can pull their own permit only if they own and occupy the residence, and they sign an owner-builder affidavit. The city also warns that a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself may be a red flag.

Buyers and their inspectors compare visible work to the record. Items the FAQ names:

  • Fences need a permit, including repair and replacement; height cannot exceed 6 feet behind the building line or 4 feet in front of it.
  • Tree removal needs a permit costing $25 regardless of how many trees, with a site plan of canopy, understory and palm trees.
  • A permit stays active only with one approved inspection every six months.

If you hold a stalled permit, ask Building Services how to close it before listing.

Who owns which pipe at a Clermont house?

The city draws a firm line. Your responsibility for water begins at the point where the line meets the city-owned water meter, and for sewer it begins where your lateral connects to the city main in the street. A leak or blockage on your side is your cost, and one on the city's side is the city's.

The FAQ also says homes with water pressure of 80 psi or more need a pressure-reducing valve under building codes, and the homeowner owns and maintains it. A failing valve or lateral shows up in inspections, so check yours before you list.

What do Clermont's emergency services look like for insurance and buyers?

The Clermont Fire Department runs four stations, at 439 W Highway 50, 2200 Hartwood Marsh Road, 2155 Legends Way and 13341 Hartle Road. The city says its units average a response time under four minutes, and Lake-Sumter EMS provides the ambulance transport.

Buyers like to hear that. It is one more detail for a listing description, and you can cite the city's own page rather than guess.

How does Florida tax a Clermont sale?

For Lake County deeds the state tax is 70 cents per $100 of the price, collected by the clerk at recording, and every signer is on the hook for it. Your closing agent can show the figure ahead of any price agreement.

Each parcel is valued on January 1, exemption applications close March 1, and a November payment earns a 4 percent discount. After a sale a homestead goes back to full just value on the next January 1, so a buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Tell buyers who compare tax records.

Can I sell a Clermont rental house with a tenant inside?

Yes, and the lease usually decides what happens next. Florida ends a month-to-month tenancy with at least 30 days of notice before a monthly period closes, a year-to-year tenancy with 60 days and a week-to-week tenancy with 7. A tenant behind on rent gets 3 days of written notice, with weekends and court holidays left out of the count.

Read the lease for an end date, deposit terms and any right of entry for showings. Some cash buyers take a rented house with the lease running, so rent keeps arriving.

What if a Clermont owner has fallen behind on the mortgage?

Foreclosures here run through the courts. After a final judgment the clerk sets a public auction for 20 to 35 days out, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. Leftover funds go to whoever claims them before the clerk reports them as unclaimed.

A lender wanting the quicker order-to-show-cause track faces a hurdle with owner-occupied homes: a homestead exemption on the latest tax roll raises a presumption that the owner lives there. Sell before the auction and the payoff comes from the proceeds, possibly leaving equity for you. Timing questions belong with a Florida attorney or your servicer.

How does probate affect selling an inherited Clermont home?

An heir cannot sell until a court gives someone authority, normally a personal representative. A non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less may use summary administration, as may one where the owner died over two years back. The revenue department lists a representative's deed under a probated will among those that owe no deed tax.

Creditors must file within three months of the first published notice, or 30 days after a known creditor is served, whichever ends last. No Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004. Agree on dates with the probate clerk and a title company before accepting an offer.

More questions about Clermont, FL

How quickly can a Clermont house sell for cash?

Often within a few weeks, because a cash buyer skips underwriting and the appraisal. Title work and liens can still set the pace. Get the offer and the closing date in writing.

Must a Clermont seller show a permit history?

A permit history is not required to list, but open permits can delay closing. Call Clermont Building Services to learn whether any permit at your address is unfinished and what inspections are needed.

What if my Clermont house has an old roof or unpermitted work?

An as-is sale is allowed, and cash buyers take houses that way. Disclose what you know, and expect a buyer to price in the repair or permit cleanup.

Who pays the Lake County deed tax?

Contracts commonly put it on the seller, though the state holds every signer liable. The charge is 70 cents per $100 of consideration; settle the point in writing.

What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?

It ends with the sale. The buyer must apply by March 1 for a new exemption, and the parcel returns to just value the following January 1.

Investors and cash buyers buy houses in Pinellas Park without a mortgage contingency, so a deal can close once the title company clears the record. A listing with an agent takes longer because a lender must approve the buyer and an appraiser must value the house.

The city's own history page shows a place built in a hurry. In 1890 F. A. Davis bought 12,800 acres on the Pinellas Peninsula, then part of West Hillsborough County, and by 1909 or 1910 a developer arrived to start a town for growing cane sugar. Pinellas County was carved out in 1913. Streets, lots and house ages here reflect more than a century of building in layers.

  • Cash route: quick answer, as-is purchase, less showing traffic.

What does Pinellas Park history say about its streets and houses?

The first newspaper issue in March 1915 mentions a Colony House at 60th Street and Park Boulevard, tent camps on Pittsburgh Avenue for arrivals waiting on homes, and a four-room brick school at 33rd Street and 7th Avenue. It also describes a drainage district covering 14,000 acres with planned canals toward Boca Ciega and Tampa Bay.

Drainage is a fair topic for a seller to prepare for. The 1915 article shows early planners treated water control as a founding project, so buyers may ask how your lot handles heavy rain, and your insurance history is the best answer you can hand them.

Which city landmarks and services do Pinellas Park buyers know?

The city history page lists the services a young town added one at a time. Library service began with the Sunshine Society in the 1920s. The city opened new library quarters at 5795 Park Boulevard in March 1959 and made the library a city department that November. Today the Barbara S. Ponce Public Library stands at 7770 52nd Street at 78th Avenue and was first dedicated March 2, 1969.

City hall has moved several times. The 1915 public school served as city hall from 1959 to 1975 and as the police department from 1975 to 1979, and it was torn down February 12, 1979. The present city hall was built in 1975. A seller can use these landmarks to describe the location of a house to out-of-town buyers.
